articleTitle: Summarization of Sanskrit Text: Approaches and Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The authors present on-going work on Text Summarizing (TS) for Sanskrit text. It is the first ever attempt towards approaches & techniques of Text Summarization for Sanskrit. It looks into the current approaches to the development of TS and suggests appropriate approaches & techniques for Sanskrit considering its peculiar features. The purpose of SATS is to concise manuscripts, improve meaning processing, and improve information retrieval processes. Although extractive text summarization (ETS) is useful, it is often not consistent, making ATS preferable for high-quality summaries. The paper reviews ATS/ETS approaches for Sanskrit and other Indian languages and suggests that a translation-based approach may be the most effective due to Sanskrit's rich morphology. A graph-based approach and supervised learning are also proposed, with future work exploring the collection of languages.

articleTitle: Wheel-Parker: Real-Time Parking Space Allocation and Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Parking has become a significant challenge in urban areas due to the increasing number of vehicles and limited spaces. Drivers often waste time and money searching for parking, which leads to traffic congestion. To address this, a prototype utilizing IoT, RFID, and IR sensors was developed. RFID captures vehicle details, IR sensors detect vehicle presence, and IoT enables remote access to parking data. The system provides real-time availability, supports advance booking, and includes theft detection. It enhances flexibility and security, making it ideal for large venues like airports and multiplexes, with minimal human intervention.

articleTitle: ADASYN: Oversampling Techniques for COVID-19 Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: In 2019, the highly contagious COVID-19 virus emerged and rapidly spread, causing a global health crisis characterized by inflammatory respiratory symptoms. The primary target of this disease is the respiratory system. Research has identified bats as the reservoir for the virus, but the intermediate host remains unknown. There is ongoing concern about various coronavirus variants, with the Omicron variant previously dominating globally and now attention shifting to a new variant, BA.2.86, informally known as Pirola, which is being closely monitored worldwide. However, the inherent class imbalance in COVID-19 datasets poses a significant obstacle to the effectiveness of these models. This paper proposes a novel approach combining outlier detection and Adaptive Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (ADASYNA) to address this issue. The Outlier-ADASYNA method identifies outliers within the minority class (COVID-19 cases) and synthesizes informative samples to rebalance the dataset. The proposed approach is evaluated using data from 5,400 patient records for both training and testing. The study employs ADASYN to effectively mitigate dataset imbalances and outstanding traditional oversampling techniques. This paper presents a comparative analysis of machine learning techniques, evaluating their performance using diverse metrics. The classification algorithm Random Forest attains the highest accuracy percentage of 90%, and RF Oversampling 92% surpassing numerous classification algorithms in predictive performance.

articleTitle: CNN-DBO: Dung Beetle Optimization Based Urban Area Change Detection Using Satellite Images
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: In recent years, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) have garnered a significant deal of interest for their ability to detect changes in metropolitan areas. One of the uses of change detection in satellite photographs is in the field of urban planning. Other applications include environmental monitoring and remote surveillance. A number of different approaches have been suggested in recent times for the purpose of automatically identifying alterations in the land cover based on GIS photographs. However, due to poor texture, cluttered context, and considerable object scale disparities, the convolutional neural network (CNN) method is only partially successful in capturing the context from geographic information systems (GISs). This is despite the fact that it remains an effective method for detecting change in urban environments. The article presents the construction of a CNN-based change detection model using the utilization of Dung Beetle Optimization (DBO). The DBO algorithm is used to adjust the loss parameter in order to increase the overall performance. The approach that was proposed makes use of the Onera satellite data set and displays an overall accuracy of 97.50% percent. In light of this, it appears that the strategy that is proposed is both very efficient and effective.

articleTitle: Improved Fuzzified LA Transformer Integrated CNN for Person Reidentification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Person re-identification is one of the challenging tasks in computer vision where the aim is to identify individuals accurately across various camera views in complex environments. Here, an advanced framework combining LA Transformer models and Convolutional Neural Networks with robust feature extraction for CNN and LA Transformer models with part-based attention mechanisms which are meant to deal with occlusion and appearance variation and aimed at extracting local features. The features extracted by the approach above are fused and refined with a Fuzzy Neural Network to integrate using fuzzy logic better features and improve classification accuracy. The proposed approach is effective due to the experimental result, which even surpasses standard approaches in challenging instances with higher Rank-1 accuracy and Mean Average Precision (mAP) for person re-identification benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: Pathology Image Classification for Colorectal Cancer Prediction Using Experience Replay
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Pathology image classification helps diagnosis and monitoring as well as treatment of a disease. Thus, it can help the decision-making of a health worker. Still, conventional machine learning models struggle with medical data that often changes, as they typically need retraining on the full dataset to learn new information on a frequent basis. This retraining requires a lot of computations and sometimes loses what it “knew” previously. This is called catastrophic forgetting. To solve this problem, we propose a continual learning framework, using Experience Replay to gradually add new pathology image data, while retaining knowledge of older tasks. Using Experience Replay, the model replays a sample of past data while training so that it does not forget any new information. The proposed framework is validated on the PathMNIST dataset, where it shows better classification accuracy and robustness than the classical retraining. This indicates that continual learning has the potential to be used for pathology image classification, and as a result, it can be scalable and adaptive to the needs of large-scale medical data. Through such advancements diagnostic accuracy will increase, resource use will become more efficient, and patient outcomes will improve in medicine.

articleTitle: Strategic Blended Learning for Addressing Multiclass Imbalance in Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Numerous practical applications involve multiclass classification challenges, where the spread of data across the classes is frequently uneven. Due to this inherent data imbalance, supervised learning models often exhibit a bias toward classifying instances into the category with the highest number of data points, posing a significant problem that requires attention. In the realm of classification of data with multiple classes and imbalanced distributions, researchers in machine learning persistently endeavor to mitigate the classifier's inclination towards dominant class with more sample size. Existing studies aim to alleviate this inclination by alternatively adjusting the data for balance prior to the classifier's learning process or adjusting the classifier's training process to focus more on rare class having least number of samples, or employing hybrid strategies. Existing learning approaches encounter challenges in delineating clear boundaries between samples of classes resulting from an imbalanced class distribution and issues with class overlapping. Consequently, the recognition rate for minority classes is hindered. A novel Strategic Blended Learning (SBL) approach is introduced, employing dual decision trees. The first decision tree is utilized to generate an induced dataset through a grouping approach, while the second decision tree is employed to train and make decisions guided by the induced dataset. A noteworthy aspect of this algorithmic approach is its ability to identify rare data points without affecting the inherent distribution of data. To evaluate the proposed algorithm, various multiclass imbalanced datasets from UCI were employed for classification. The findings revealed that the Strategic Blended Learning method excels in detecting both rare and dominant category samples.

articleTitle: Exploring the Adoption of Wearable Technologies by Employees of Ed Tech Sector and Its Impact on Productivity: A Perspective Through the Theory of Gratification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The researchers have utilized the Theory of Gratification as a framework to gauge the adoption intention and hence the impact on productivity by embracing wearable technologies by the employees of Ed Tech sector. The proposed theoretical model has highlighted the impact of Workplace safety (WPS), Curiosity (CUR), Convenience (CON), Social Influence (SOI) and Trialability (TRB) on Adoption Intention (ADI) and productivity of employees. Moderating impact of Trust on the above-mentioned factors have also been validated by using SPSS and AMOS. Theory of Gratification has corroborated the primary responses collected from the employees of Ed Tech sector pertaining in the Bangalore region (n=377). The results arrived at by using Structural Equation Model (SEM) analysis suggest that there exists a significant positive relationship between ADI & WPS, ADI & CUR, ADI & CON, ADI & SOI, ADI & TRI. The moderation results signify that trust moderates the relationship between WPS & ADI, Con & ADI. This study will facilitate the Education sector to arrive at informed decision-making and embrace new technology for the wellbeing of its employees.

articleTitle: Multi Disease Prediction Related to Pulmonary Area by Leveraging Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: A large portion of the world's healthcare issues are related to conditions that impact the chest, heart, lungs, and respiratory system, which affect millions of people annually. To address this issue, we present the Deep learning-based model, which will detect multi diseases related to pulmonary condition. Multi pulmonary areas disease can be detected if the disease is present in the dataset of X- rays and CT Scans photos. This research shows the count of diseases out of the whole dataset taken. Its motive is to predict multi diseases related to the pulmonary area. This research will help the radiologists to make a quick diagnosis of pulmonary disease conditions. Ultimately, it will help the patients to have an earlier idea about disease to take treatment on time.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity With Blockchain: Strengthening the Privacy and Security of Data in Internet of Things Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The explosion of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has changed the way people interact with technology by making data-driven decisions and smart environments feasible. The exponential growth in the number of linked devices has also increased the attack surface for cyber assaults, leading to significant concerns about the privacy and security of Internet of Things networks. Conventional security measures aren't always up to the task of dealing with the unique challenges posed by the Internet of Things (IoT), such as resource scarcity, unpredictable network topologies, and the generation of massive volumes of data. Increasing the cybersecurity posture of Internet of Things networks is the focus of this research, which investigates the possibility of incorporating blockchain technology as a promising solution. We propose a novel design that leverages the immutability, decentralization, and data encryption features of blockchain technology to secure data from the Internet of Things (IoT). Using smart contracts to automate security protocols, the framework creates a trustless environment where Internet of Things devices can securely share information. We analyze common Internet of Things weaknesses such as the framework's ability to prevent data modification, unauthorized access. We undertake a detailed examination of the performance of the framework. All things considered, our research shows that the blockchain-based approach greatly improves the privacy and security of IoT data. Decentralized consensus methods fortify the system against weak points, and an immutable ledger ensures that all data transfers are secure. Access control and authentication procedures are simplified by the utilization of smart contracts, which in turn reduces the likelihood of unauthorized data breaches occurring. Both the scalability and processing overhead concerns that are involved with the application of blockchain technology in Internet of Things networks are addressed by this research. We offer optimization methods to overcome these challenges, so the suggested framework will remain functional and beneficial for Internet of Things applications in the actual world. This research provides strong evidence in support of using blockchain technology to secure Internet of Things networks. The proposed architecture not only strengthens the cybersecurity infrastructure, but also allows for the creation of more private and secure Internet of Things applications. Findings from this study add to the continuing efforts to safeguard the digital environment against cyber threats that are always developing.

articleTitle: Coronary Heart Disease Prediction Using CNN, RNN, LSTM and Attention DNN Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Coronary Heart Disease popularly referred to as CHD is one of the leading causes of death and illness across the global population making it imperative for the identification of an effective approach to its predictive modeling for early detection. The purpose of this research includes studying a dataset containing a variety of clinical characteristics in order to forecast CHD using sophisticated deep learning structures. Specifically, we implemented and evaluated four distinct models: Convolutional Neural Networks, Long Short-Term Memory networks, Recurrent Neural Networks and Attention Deep Neural Networks (DNN). All models are trained and evaluated on data set and multiple performance measures like accuracy, recall, precision, and F1score were used for the purpose. The experimental outcome showed that the Attention-based DNN had the highest accuracy rate of 91 % followed by the RNN with accuracy rate of 89%. CNN and LSTM models gave moderate accuracy but they did not outperform the best models among options.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Sensorsless Automated Guided Vehicle for Small Warehouse Rack Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Automated guided vehicles (AGVs) are an essential part of today's logistics networks because they save time, reduce wear and maintenance expenses, and maximize efficiency in route design.The creation of AGVthat is capable of effectively managing warehouse racks without the utilization of sensors is the primary emphasis of this project. In order to travel and carry out duties, the AGVruns on predetermined pathways and makes use of a button-based interface. For the purpose of offering an efficient and costeffective solution for the automation of small warehouses, it is outfitted with a lever mechanism that is operated by a servo motor and features the ability to connect and move racks.

articleTitle: InceptionV3-Driven Multiclassifier Voting System for Watermark Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Watermark text detection and classification are fundamental tasks in computer vision. This study addresses the challenge of classifying watermarked versus non-watermarked text in natural scene images by utilizing the InceptionV3 model for feature extraction. We evaluate the performance of three clas-sifiers— k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest (RF)—in distinguishing between these text types across two distinct datasets. By applying our method to these datasets, we ensure a comprehensive evaluation and assess the robustness of our approach. The results underscore the effectiveness of the InceptionV3 model in capturing relevant features, followed by a comparative analysis of the classifiers based on accuracy, precision, and recall. To further enhance classification performance, a weighted voting decision mechanism is employed, leveraging the strengths of each classifier. The weighted voting accuracy for Dataset1 and Dataset2 are 95.02% and 92.72%, respectively. The weighted voting approach com-bines individual classifier predictions based on their performance metrics, resulting in improved accuracy and more balanced classification results.

articleTitle: Accelerating Efficient Adsorption Energy Calculations Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Design of catalysis is important for various sustainable purposes like enhancing reaction rates in industrial process, improving the overall yield of desired products, reducing harmful emissions in chemical manufacturing. Adsorption energy plays major role in understanding strength of catalyst by analysing reaction mechanism at molecular level. In this research adsorbML algorithm is used to identify low-energy adsorbate-surface configurations more accurately and efficiently. It uses fc100 dataset for catalyst analysis. This study demonstrates the low energy adsorbate-surface configurations of Au and Ni alloys by using ASE, LFGBS, algorithms for finding force values, and show the relaxation process over time. From this analysis Ni and Au adsorption energy is 2.28 eV and 2.00 eV at 100 and 79<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> step. Similarly the minimum binding energy (adsorption energy) for any adsorbate-surface combination is found using this adsorbML algorithm.

articleTitle: Advancing Underwater Image Enhancement Using Hybrid Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: When attempting to make underwater images better, there are a lot of obstacles to overcome, including water's inherent color distortion, inadequate visibility, and light absorption and dispersion noise. The difficulties in accurately analyzing images caused by these problems apply to marine research, underwater robots, and environmental monitoring are only a few areas which are impacted. To address the limitations of existing picture enhancement techniques, this paper proposes a new hybrid deep learning CNN + GAN model for enhancing underwater photographs. The hybrid model extracts features with GANs and noise reduces with CNNs to produce better photos with better clarity and color correction. I train and validate the model using an underwater picture dataset and it defeats the state of the art approaches on visibility, color correctness, contrast and contrast. In quantitative and qualitative assessments our hybrid deep learning method yields superior generalization in different undersea environments relative to traditional methods. A suggested approach can potentially improve the underwater photography, marine setting data collecting with more precision, as well as better underwater exploration. This work now provides confidence in research progress into autonomous underwater exploration systems and underwater image processing.

articleTitle: Classification of Millet Cultivars Using Image Processing and Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: India is one of the leading producers of various millet cultivars. Indian millets are a class of highly nutritious, drought-resistant crops that are mostly cultivated in the country's semi-arid and drought-prone regions. The most popularly cultivated millet varieties in India are Sorghum (Jowar), Pearl millet (Bajra), Barnyard Millet (Bhagar), Foxtail millet (Kangi), Amaranth (Rajgira), Red sorghum (Chikani), Finger millet (Nachani), and White sorghum (Dadar). In addition to being a wholesome dietary source, millets offer several health advantages. Since they don't contain gluten, they're an excellent alternative for anyone with gluten sensitivity or coeliac disease. Additionally low in glycemic index; millets are a great meal choice for diabetics. Each cultivar has a different nutritional composition and uses. Also, the majority of the time the farmers adapted the millet seeds obtained from their crop hence to preserve the purity of seeds and quality of produce it is very important to classify different millet cultivars. However, the classification of millet cultivars is a complex and time-consuming process. Automation in millet cultivar classification becomes greatly beneficial with improved accuracy and efficiency. This study presents the effective classification of eight different millet cultivars using different machine-learning classifiers along with image processing techniques, based on the derived color features.

articleTitle: Enhancing Career Development: An AI-Driven Mentorship Platform for Student-Mentor Connections
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Thunai is an AI-powered mentorship platform that connects users with personalized mentors for career guidance. Key features include automated calendar booking, video communication with privacy-enhancing dynamic emojis, and AI-driven mentor matching aligned with mentee goals. The AI assistant, GURU, supports task management, resource recommendations, and LinkedIn-based evaluations to foster growth. Thunai offers subscription plans and partnerships with educational and mental health organizations, enhancing engagement, leadership development, and networking. Leveraging AI technologies like sentiment analysis and feedback, Thunai improves mentor matching, user satisfaction, and mentee engagement for career and emotional well-being.

articleTitle: Computing Midcurve with Multi-Layer and Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Midcurve computation: the dimension reduction of 2D thin polygon shapes to 1D curves is important for several Computer-Aided Design (CAD) and Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE) applications, particularly in finite element analysis and robot path planning. We advance the state-of-the-art by building on previous work on MidcurveNN, through two new neural architectures: a multi-layer dense network and a CNN-based architecture with skip connections. Through comparative analysis, we demonstrate that while the dense network shows limited improvements, the CNN-based architecture with skip connections achieves a tenfold reduction in average loss compared to existing methods. The proposed approach improves the quality of the generated Midcurves.

articleTitle: Systolic Array Design for Efficient FPGA Implementation of CNN Accelerators: Power and Area Optimizations
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are widely used in image processing, object detection, and other machine learning applications due to their ability to extract features from data effectively. However, the high computational and memory demands of CNNs pose significant challenges for real-time ap plications, especially in resource constrained environments such as edge devices where power consumption is a critical factor. This project proposes the design and implementation of a power efficient heterogeneous systolic array architecture integrated with low-power techniques to accelerate CNN operations. The design aims to optimize resource utilization and throughput while reducing power consumption. By leveraging specialized processing elements (PEs) and efficient dataflow methods, the proposed architecture seeks to achieve substantial improvements in power efficiency and performance compared to traditional systolic arrays.

articleTitle: Black Hole Attack Detection Using Dynamic Threshold Values and Residual Energy in VANETs
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: In black hole attack, a hostile vehicle or node within the VANET pretends to have the optimal route to the destination, convincing other nodes to route their data packets through it as they head towards the destination, trailing behind the malicious node, receives the data, it either discards the packets completely or forwards them selectively, causing disruptions in communication. To overcome this dilemma the research discusses a novel approach for categorizing nodes in AODV (Adhoc On demand vector Routing Protocol) networks according to their residual energy (RE) and forward rate (FR). With the goal to identify nodes that are considered energy-constrained, the proposed approach defines a residual energy threshold (RET) and includes dynamic threshold values (MinDTV and MaxDTV) for the forward rate. Three categories are applied to nodes: 1. (Trusted), 2. (Intermediate), and 3. (Untrusted or Energy-Constrained). This methodology results in a more trustworthy and energy-efficient network by dynamically updating node selection based on present forwarding behavior and levels of energy. The proposed approach boosts the overall strength, longevity as well, and integrity of RPL networks through the elimination of energy-depleted and unstable nodes; hence, it is especially suitable for applications in scenarios with scarce resources and malicious activity.

articleTitle: Mathematical Capabilities of LLMs
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have the potential to solve mathematical problems well, but little has been investigated. In this research, we evaluate five leading LLMs — (Gemini, Claude, Mistral, ChatGPT, and Llama — on a set of 50 mathematical problems that cover calculus, algebra, geometry, number theory, and probability. Finally, the study evaluates the accuracy of their solutions and gives the ability to assess their intermediate steps correctly. I created a primary dataset for comparison of the LLM performances and ranked the models according to how well they were able to solve those problems. It illustrates the shortcomings of present LLMs at reasoning and solving for mathematics and suggests what needs to be rectified in the LLMs. Future research will further refine this dataset and monitor the progression of LLM capabilities in solving more complex mathematical problems.

articleTitle: An Approach of ML & DL to Analyze Brain Tumor Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Accurate brain tumor prediction in MRI images is a critical aspect of modern neuro-oncology, significantly impacting patient outcomes through early diagnosis and targeted treatment. In this paper, we explore how to improve detection and classification by applying traditional ML and DL techniques such as CNN. Integrating data augmentation, transfer learning, and advanced image pre-processing techniques has further refined model performance, enabling the practical analysis of low-quality MRI scans. However, challenges remain in ensuring model interpretability and addressing class imbalance in training datasets. This study highlights the current landscape of tumor detection methodologies using ML and DL, emphasizing models that provide high accuracy and offer transparent decision-making processes. By synthesizing findings from various research efforts, to assist the challenging task of brain tumor identification in medical science, this paper aims to contribute to the ongoing development of AI-driven diagnostic tools.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Algorithm for Sensitive Data Classification on Cloud Environment
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: This electronic Digital information, computer systems, networks, and data are highly in need of protection from damage, unauthorized access, and internal and external threats. Cyber security involves the implementation of strong procedures to protect digital resources by ensuring confidentiality, integrity, and availability. In the dynamic landscape of cyberspace, Cyber security is the umbrella term for tactics, tools, and procedures used to fend off a wide variety of threats, such as ransomware, phishing, malware, and other unwanted activity. This field continually evolves to counter emerging risks and vulnerabilities, requiring a proactive approach to identify, assess, and moderate potential security breaches. Cyber security is fundamental in preserving trust and reliability in digital interactions, serving as a critical component in our interconnected and technology-driven world. Here we focused on the large amount of data set to identify the level of confidentiality required and categories them using machine learning approaches. The results will be carryied forward for the high computational encryption and decryption to provide high security and provide access as per the need of the users.

articleTitle: Factors Influencing the Customer Satisfaction and WOM (Word of Mouth) of Smart Watches: A Perspective of Technology Acceptance Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The researchers have adopted Technology Acceptance Model (TAM3) to gauze the customer satisfaction level and WOM for smartwatches. The paper intends to examine the factors which influence the adoption intention, customer satisfaction and WOM of smartwatches. TAM3 model was used to validate the primary data comprising of 383 respondents which was further examined by SEM. The findings of the result revealed that motivation and innovation influence the perceived ease of use (PEU). Compatibility and social influence significantly impacted PUF (perceived usefulness). Both PEU and PUF significantly impacted the adoption intention of smartwatches. The adoption intention was positively connected with customer satisfaction which in turn led to word of mouth (WOM) . The study will help the smartwatch manufacturers gain deep insight understanding the factors influencing customer satisfaction and generation of word-of-mouth publicity

articleTitle: Effectiveness Assessment of Different Deep Learning Architectures for Sentiment Analysis on Twitter During COVID-19
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: People are sharing their opinions, feelings, and attitudes about many aspects of the COVID-19 pandemic on Twitter, where social media activity has surged. In order to find the optimum approach, this study compares different deep learning architectures for sentiment analysis of COVID-19-related tweets. This article makes use of a large dataset of tweets concerning the COVID-19 pandemic, encompassing a wide range of opinions, from neutral to unfavorable. Thorough preprocessing of the dataset is carried out, including tokenization, removal of stop words, and application of methods such as word embedding to store semantic information in compact vector representations of words. Examined in this comparative study were three deep learning architectures that saw extensive use: RNNs, CNNs, and transformer-based models. Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score are some of the appropriate performance metrics that are used to train and evaluate each architecture. When it comes to conducting sentiment analysis on tweets pertaining to COVID-19, our experimental results provide useful insights into the efficiency and effectiveness of different deep learning architectures. Although all deep learning architectures demonstrate sentiment analysis capability, the study found that some designs offered better accuracy and sentiment prediction capabilities than others. Transformer-based models, such as the famous BERT architecture, perform quite well, particularly when it comes to understanding the complex sentiment dynamics in tweets and absorbing contextual information.

articleTitle: Plant Leaf Disease Classification and Identification Using Deep Convolution Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: With the advancement of deep learning, and CNNs in particular, comes the ability to correctly classify plant diseases automatically with increased accuracy. This work provides a robust system by adopting CNN architectures and employing the application of transfer learning toward leaf disease classification in plants using diverse datasets, with proper preprocessing and augmentation. Deployed as a user-friendly application, the system demonstrates significant potential in enhancing crop productivity and minimizing losses through early disease detection.

articleTitle: RF and IoT-Driven Automated Lane Clearance System for Enhanced Emergency Response
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: In urban areas, traffic congestion often causes significant delays in emergency response times, potentially jeopardizing lives. This project proposes an Automatic Lane Clearance System specifically designed to facilitate the swift movement of ambulances through traffic. The system employs a combination of IoT and RF-based technologies, enabling real-time communication between ambulances, nearby vehicles, and traffic signal infrastructure. The ambulance unit is equipped with an Arduino microcontroller, RF transmitter, Node MCU (ESP8266) for Wi-Fi communication, and an LCD display. The system utilizes UBIDOTS as the IoT platform for data logging and monitoring, powered by a dedicated battery supply to ensure continuous operation. When an ambulance approaches a high-traffic area, the RF transmitter signals nearby vehicles, equipped with RF receivers and Arduino microcontrollers, to clear a path. Simultaneously, the system communicates with the traffic signal infrastructure via Node MCU, triggering the traffic lights to display a green signal for the ambulance route. Additionally, a buzzer alert is activated at the traffic signal to notify pedestrians and other vehicles of the emergency situation. This automated lane clearance system aims to reduce response time by ensuring that ambulances encounter minimal resistance in their path. By utilizing an efficient communication protocol across multiple traffic entities, the system promises a reliable and scalable solution for emergency traffic management in smart city initiatives.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Liquid Level Monitoring and Control System for Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Storage vessels play a crucial role in the chemical industry by accommodating a wide range of solvents, including those that are toxic, volatile, or hazardous. It is essential for process engineers to maintain optimal liquid levels for various unit operations, making continuous fluid level monitoring a necessity. Failure to monitor the liquid level in a tank appropriately can lead to spills and potentially dangerous accidents. Inadequate liquid levels can also result in vessel damage and operational disruptions. In this study, we have developed a real-time liquid level monitoring system that calculates and transmits data to a remote server via a wireless network. This IoT-based monitoring system is constructed using components such as the ESP32 microcontroller, HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor module, LCD display, and motor driver unit. This system sends real-time data to a central server, allowing multiple users to access the current level and quantity of chemicals or solvents. Furthermore, our system offers remote valve control capabilities through IoT technology, enabling users to open or close inlet and outlet valves remotely, and even automate these actions. This work provides significant benefits to process engineers, as it offers live updates on liquid levels, which can be conveniently accessed from their workstations or mobile devices, enhancing safety and efficiency in chemical industry operations.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis Using Categorical Boosting Classifier (CatBoost), Ensemble Hard Voting Classifier (EHVC) & Convolution Neural Network (CNN) for DNA Sequence Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Recently, Machine Learning (ML) has become an essential methodology for medical science. Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA) carries all the genetic information of every individual. The extraction of features from DNA genetic variations & identifying species are quite difficult without using ML and deep learning as it can learn the features automatically. It cannot process the raw data as DNA sequences are represented as the combination of adenine (A), thymine (T), guanine (G) & cytosine (C). A conversion of string data to a tokenized vector is needed as it mapped with nucleotides to a numerical token. A k-mer substring of length k hexamer words of size 6 is used here as its coming from a longer DNA sequence with a combination of ATGC. In this paper, the Categorical Boosting classifier (CatBoost), an ensemble algorithm with hard voting, is proposed with the combination of K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF) model together to make better accuracy and robustness of the DNA classification task after vectorization of k hexamer of 6 word sizes. These enable the correctness of medicine, early disease diagnosis, and genomic observation of infectious diseases. The proposed model also integrates the deep learning model, which consists of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), to improve the accuracy of DNA sequence classification over the CatBoost and the EHVC. Our model accuracy of the ensemble method using hard voting achieved 93% and CNN 95%.

articleTitle: Real-Time Gender Classification Using MiniXception and Hand Gesture Detection Using MediaPipe Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: In human-computer interaction, gender classification and hand gesture recognition are essential technologies. This paper presents a real-time system that integrates gender prediction and face and hand gesture detection, utilising the Mini Xception model and MediaPipe framework. We address the requirements for efficient real-time operation by utilizing frame-skipping mechanisms in our work. The system comprises video capture with OpenCV, model integration using TensorFlow, and efficient data handling with NumPy. Extensive testing has proven its generalization to diverse settings and excellent performance, with 84% accuracy for both tasks, capable of real-time processing.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Comparison of Machine Learning Classification Techniques for Early Detection of Alzheimer's Disorder
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Alzheimer's disorder (AlzD) is a chronic condition in which brain cells degenerate and eventually die. People over the age of 65 are most likely to get this condition. There is no cure for this, but nowadays proper medications and treatments are available to slow down the disease progression temporarily. Detection of AlzD in its early stage may help doctors and physicians provide proper medicines as early as possible to slow its development. Artificial intelligence is a blooming field in every sector nowadays that can help in AlzD detection to save us from time-consuming and expensive conventional methods. Various machine learning algorithms are researched to prevent AlzD. This paper uses different linear, distance, and tree-based supervised classifier algorithms. The used dataset contains different psychological parameters like a person's age, number of visits, Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), and years of education, on which machines can be trained to predict whether the person is demented or non-demented. The main goal of this research paper is to compare these classification algorithms which give the best result in the early detection of AlzD. RFC, KNN, and MLP algorithms outperform all other algorithms with an accuracy of 96.77<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, followed by NB and LR algorithms with 95.70%.

articleTitle: Metaheuristic Approaches in Path Finding and Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Navigation planning is a critical component in the operation of mobile systems such as robots, autonomous vehicles, and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). As the complexity of these systems increases, the need for robust and efficient pathfinding algorithms becomes more significant. Traditional heuristic approaches often struggle in dynamic environments, prompting the adoption of metaheuristic algorithms inspired by natural phenomena. This study evaluates five widely used metaheuristic algorithms: Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), Firefly Algorithm (FA), Moth Flame Optimization (MFO), and Tabu Search (TS). The performance of these algorithms is compared across multiple scenarios, including static shortest-path calculations, the Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP), and randomized environment. Results indicate that ACO consistently identifies optimal paths but incurs relatively high computational time. Tabu Search offers a balanced trade-off between computational efficiency and solution quality, while ABC delivers suboptimal paths with faster execution times. In contrast, MFO and FA exhibit excessive exploration, leading to higher costs and inefficiencies in specific scenarios.

articleTitle: Optimizing Network Lifetime in Wireless Sensor Networks Through Efficient Data Transmission
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are integral to modern applications ranging from environmental monitoring to military operations. Despite their utility, the limited energy capacity of sensor nodes remains a critical challenge, particularly during the most energy-intensive task of data transmission. This paper introduces a novel clustering-based communication protocol designed to optimize energy efficiency and extend the network lifetime. Unlike traditional protocols such as LEACH and SEP, the proposed algorithm minimizes redundant data transmission by employing a control mechanism that detects and skips identical data in successive rounds. This innovation reduces energy consumption during communication between non-cluster head nodes, cluster heads (CHs), and the base station (BS). Simulations conducted in static, semi-dynamic, and dynamic environments demonstrate significant improvements in network stability, energy efficiency, and overall lifespan. These results position the proposed protocol as a robust solution for energy-constrained WSNs.

articleTitle: Enhancing NLP for Indic Languages With Limited Resources: A Study of Transformer Models for Translation and Summarization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Significant advancements have been made in natural language processing (NLP), especially in numerous languages. The vast linguistic diversity of India presents unique challenges for automated language processing tasks as Indian languages other than Hindi are marginalized in both cases; datasets which incur a vast toll on summarization models that require huge datasets to be trained on. This paper presents a comparative and comprehensive analysis of multiple transformer-based models which have been trained and/or fine-tuned for lesser-used Indic languages. Purely focusing on Natural Language Translation (NLT) and evaluating its efficiency in generating contextually accurate summaries for languages such as Bengali and Marathi. Models such as mT5, IndicBART, mBART and other multilingual NLP models will be benchmarked and assessed using the ROUGE score. This study highlights the model's strengths and weaknesses in handling the limitations summarization of low-resource Indic languages. The findings will contribute heavily to the development of NLP tools aimed at improving summarization inclusivity across India's diverse languages.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure and Dc-Dc Converter Control Towards Sustainable Transportation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The rise of electric vehicles (EVs) has marked a significant shift towards sustainable transportation, necessitating the development of robust charging infrastructure and efficient power management systems. This paper explores the pivotal role of electric vehicle charging infrastructure in facilitating widespread EV adoption and examines challenges such as grid capacity constraints and interoperability standards. Additionally, it delves into the role of DC-DC converters in optimizing power flow and efficiency in EV charging systems. By harnessing renewable energy sources like solar and wind, eco-friendly charging stations offer a promising solution to reduce greenhouse gas emissions while meeting the escalating demand for EV charging. Through innovation and strategic policy initiatives, the electrification of transportation holds the promise of reshaping urban landscapes and paving the way towards a more sustainable future.

articleTitle: The Utilization of Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI) with CLONALG to Amplify Exhibited Neurological Signals
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Nearly 50 million individuals are diagnosed with neurodegenerative diseases every year. Moreover, this figure is expected to grow as the population grows older. These neurodegenerative diseases have had a profound impact on the neurological functioning of an individual. For instance, being diagnosed with cerebral palsy has been correlated with poor movement and coordination, atypical development patterns, and communication and swallowing difficulties. To help these struggling individuals, scientists have developed a plethora of technologies to assimilate them into day-to-day life. For example, botox injections are commonly used to relieve muscle spasms that have prevented swallowing difficulties. However, these existing treatments have all had disadvantages. For example, botox injections have commonly led to side effects, such as a crooked smile, watery and dry eyes, and flu-like symptoms. Overall, these side effects have disrupted individuals' psychological state, causing renewed calls for better treatments. Fortunately, brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) provide hope for these individuals. For example, to minimize the consequences of cerebral palsy, brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) allow for the usage of remaining muscular pathways as a substitute for paralyzed muscles. This substitution allows for the eyes and hands to have renewed control over communication devices. In this research paper, we will analyze techniques to optimize the strength of brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) by specifically analyzing how the CLONALG algorithm will enhance the strength of brain-computer interfaces.

articleTitle: Development of Assistance System for Online Dispute Resolution and Legal Advice Using AIML
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: In the present work, the main goal is to reduce the downsides of litigation and other traditional conflict resolution procedures. Many people and corporations avoid litigation due to its high costs, extended timelines, and mental stress. This methodology presents a fresh perspective on conflict resolution, one that makes use of technology to simplify the process and provides an affordable and easily accessible option. At the heart of this strategy is an Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) platform that allows for the digital resolution of disputes, doing away with the necessity for physical presence and the expenses that come along with it. Everyone from sole proprietors to large corporations, regardless of their level of legal knowledge, may utilize the platform because to its intuitive design. Eventually, this initiative seeks to enable individuals and companies to confidently and easily manage legal difficulties by reshaping the landscape of legal dispute resolution with an emphasis on speed, accessibility, and openness. Reduced legal fees, reduced time to resolution, and less emotional toll on parties are just a few of the many advantages of this strategy. People with private legal issues and small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs) resolving business conflicts are among our project's intended users.

articleTitle: Development of Interactive Assistance for Academic Preparation Using Large Models Language
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: With the increase in capabilities and availability of large language models, it is inevitable that it finds its way into application in a variety of domains. Education domain has seen remarkable improvements in both efficiency and capabilities with the incorporation of innovative and latest technology to improve the experience for both teachers as well as students and when talking about latest technologies it is impossible to not talk about large language models. Their ability to contemplate huge volumes of data as well as generate human-like responses to queries related to data it possesses has made many industries rethink certain aspects of their workflow to integrate this powerful technology to improve the working efficiency. Education sector can benefit from this technology in various aspects. This project aims to integrate the usage of locally run large language models using Ollama and LangChain to build a conversational platform application for the usage by students for assisted learning. The model also utilizes Retrieval Augmented generation techniques for creating an updated and dynamic large language model. To promote transparency stateof-the-art open-source technologies are preferred rather than closed source technologies like OpenAI's ChatGPT.

articleTitle: Enhancing Software Vulnerability Detection Using Code Property Graphs and Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The increasing complexity of modern software sys- tems has led to a rise in vulnerabilities that malicious actors can exploit. Traditional methods of vulnerability detection, such as static and dynamic analysis, have limitations in scalability and automation. This paper proposes a novel approach to detecting software vulnerabilities using a combination of code property graphs and machine learning techniques. By leveraging code property graphs, which integrate abstract syntax trees, control flow graphs, and program dependency graphs, we achieve a detailed representation of software code that enhances the accuracy and granularity of vulnerability detection. We intro- duce various neural network models, including convolutional neural networks adapted for graph data, to process these rep- resentations. Our approach provides a scalable and automated solution for vulnerability detection, addressing the shortcomings of existing methods. We also present a newly generated dataset labeled with function-level vulnerability types sourced from open- source repositories. Our contributions include a methodology for transforming software code into code property graphs, the implementation of a convolutional neural network model for graph data, and the creation of a comprehensive dataset for training and evaluation. This work lays the foundation for more effective and efficient vulnerability detection in complex software systems.

articleTitle: Leveraging EfficientNet-B0 for Soybean Leaf Disease Detection: A Deep Learning Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Plant diseases require quick and accurate identification methods since they significantly reduce agricultural production's output and quality. Traditional methods of plant protection, which depend on visual assessment of pests and diseases that impact soyabean plants, have long turnaround times and variable accuracy. A critical need as the demand for precision agriculture grows is the creation of quick, effective, and—above all—computer-aided disease recognition systems. This study proposed convolutional neural network-based classification model for soyabean leaf. Proposed model can detect nine different types of soyabean diseases. Our transfer-learning based model classifies soybean leaves using a Inception B0 convolutional neural network, and on unseen testing data, we obtain balanced accuracies between 91.11% and 96.44%. The result of proposed model is generated on 3000 different images of soyabean leaves and classify nine different types of soyabean diseases.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Deep Learning for Automated Wheat Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The title “AI-Driven Deep Learning for Automated Wheat Disease Detection” points to a major change in how we identify wheat diseases. Crop diseases are a major cause of reduced agricultural yields and contribute significantly to global economic losses in the farming sector. To mitigate these effects, it is essential to monitor and manage crop health effectively. Diagnosing wheat diseases involves figuring out what's affecting the plants, whether it's fungi, bacteria, or other harmful organisms. Accurate diagnosis is essential for safeguarding crops and helping farmers achieve a healthy and productive harvest. Here we use the advanced and powerful technologies like deep learning and Artificial Intelligence. For wheat farming, AI can swiftly and precisely identify diseases in plants. Deep Learning, a branch of AI, improves by analysing large amounts of data, like images of healthy and sick wheat. In earlier research, image classification for disease detection relied on manually designed features. However, recent advancements in Deep Learning have significantly enhanced the precision of object detection and classification. This research focuses on developing a deep learning model to identify wheat diseases from images captured directly in the field. Along with the detection of 15 various diseases of the wheat crop it also suggest the suitable pesticide. This research helps to build more accurate outputs than the earlier research by using advanced technologies.

articleTitle: Muscle Fatigue Detection Using sEMG Signals for Enhanced Prosthetic Control
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: This work explores muscle fatigue detection using surface electromyography (sEMG) signals from multiple muscle channels during prolonged load settings. Four vital temporal features, namely Root Mean Square, Waveform Length, Mean Absolute Value, and Zero Crossing, were examined across eight channels to determine the onset and progression of fatigue. The outcomes highlight the benefits of incorporating amplitude and variability-based features to provide robust real-time fatigue monitoring in Myoelectric Control Systems (MEC) and Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) applications.

articleTitle: Ai-Based Web Application Firewall
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Web applications face an increasing risk of webbased attacks such as SQL Injection (SQLi) and Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), making the need for securing them more important than ever. This project focuses on building an AIpowered Web Application Firewall (WAF) that can identify and block such attacks using machine learning in real-time. We used publicly available datasets from Kaggle and performed preprocessing steps such as text cleaning and count vectorization to make the data analysis-ready. The models used include Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine (SVM). For SQLi, Logistic Regression achieved 96.83% accuracy, while for XSS, Random Forest achieved 99.88%. These models were embedded in a web application that takes user input, and the backend evaluates it to determine if it is a safe or malicious query, providing quick feedback. These results demonstrate that AI-powered firewalls can effectively detect and block SQLi and XSS attacks in web applications, helping secure them against data loss. We approached the project of protecting web apps from vulnerabilities through machine learning to provide a scalable solution and explore ML within cybersecurity.

articleTitle: Smart AI-Based Delivery Robot
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Humans are responsible for the majority of delivering the packets over the area of a network. When compared to classic delivery system the Autonomous Delivery Robot(ADR's) is meant to deliver the goods instead of a human involvement. The delivery robots are a contact-less and alternative to human interaction. At their core, we design a budget-friendly prototype for an Autonomous Delivery Robot (ADR) that can deliver packages to their destinations safely. This robot uses a GPS (like a car's navigation system) to find its way around. We use a special kind of computer brain called Artificial Intelligence to understand the best way to go. Once delivery robot know the right path, it follows until it reaches to the final stop. The robot keeps packets secure by putting them in a special container that needs a secret code to open. The secret code to open the container can be sent to the customer mobile when they order something. Once the robot delivers your package, it can find its own way back to where it started.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Depression Detection System: Integrating Multimodal Analysis for Early Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Depression is a prevalent mental health condition affecting millions globally, often going undiagnosed due to social stigma and limited accessibility to healthcare. This study presents an innovative AI-enhanced system for early depression detection, utilizing multimodal analysis integrating natural language processing (NLP) and patient health metrics. Two machine learning models form the system's core: a text classification model leveraging logistic regression to analyze user inputs and predict emotional tone and a health-data-based model that incorporates factors such as BMI, blood features, and comorbid conditions for comprehensive evaluation. The models were integrated into a web application offering a dual advantage of accurate screening and accessible mental health recommendations. Results demonstrated high efficacy with classification accuracy exceeding 91% across models, underscoring its potential to transform early-stage mental health interventions. Future enhancements include adopting advanced deep learning frameworks and expanding multilingual capabilities to broaden accessibility.

articleTitle: Identification of Diabetes Level Using AI/ML Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Diabetes has become a critical public health challenge due to its alarming prevalence and severe complications. Predictive models are required for early diabetes detection to mitigate the impacts. The present study used K-nearest neighbor algorithm assessment regarding how age, body mass index, blood pressure, and physical activity affect diabetogenic risk. The different health data analyzed prove the effectiveness of K-NN for diagnosing those who are prone to diabetes. The model tries to classify people based on the above-named critical health indicators. Age and body mass index have an above average influence on blood pressure and amount of physical activity according to the K-NN model, thus this model could be used for effective stratification of risk related to diabetes as it scored 0.96. This confirms the utility of K-NN in providing very insightful information for assessing diabetes risk.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Encoder-Based and Decoder-Based Architectures for Automatic Conspiracy Theory Identification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: This study evaluates the performance of encoder-based and decoder-based architectures for the Automatic Con-spiracy Theory Identification (ACTI) task, focusing on Subtask A, which involves detecting conspiratorial content in Telegram posts. I compared RoBERTa-based encoder models and OpenAI GPT-2 decoder models; both fine-tuned with uniform hyperparameters. My encoder-only model achieved an Fl-score of 0.8211, while the decoder-only model reached 0.7464, both significantly outperforming the Kaggle baseline (0.5107) but falling short of the EVALITA winners' score of 0.8572. The encoder model showed stronger performance in identifying conspiratorial content with fewer false positives, whereas the decoder model struggled with an increased number of false negatives. The results underscore the encoder-based model's effectiveness in this context and contribute to understanding the strengths and limitations of these architectures for conspiracy theory detection

articleTitle: Design an Approach for Epileptic Seizure Detection Using EEG Patterns and Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Examining electroencephalogram (EEG) signals plays a crucial role in monitoring brain activity for diagnosing various conditions, with primary applications in detecting epileptic seizures and sleep disorders. Given the diverse range of EEG seizure patterns, there is a significant need to differentiate between normal and seizure data. This study proposes the extraction of time domain statistical and frequency features from EEG signals to enhance classification accuracy. A FIR filter is suggested as a preliminary step to remove artifacts from EEG signals. The research introduces a wavelet-based classifier for extracting EEG frequency features and contributes to the calculation of temporal statistical features using wavelet-based classifications. The study aims to categorize EEG signal patterns into Z, N, F, and S types. Power spectral density (PSD) and peak-to-peak difference (PPD) are utilized as specialized features for classification purposes. Additionally, temporal mean and entropy of EEG signals are employed as statistical features. This expanded feature set can be effectively used in machine learning (ML) based EEG pattern classification, achieving a maximum accuracy of 96.7%.

articleTitle: Optimization-Based Hyperparameter Tuning Using Extra Trees to Classify Type-2-Diabetes Mellitus
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The increasing prevalence of diabetes mellitus (DM) is impacting an ever-growing number of households globally. Many individuals diagnosed with diabetes have limited awareness of their health status and associated risk factors prior to diagnosis. This study introduces a novel approach utilizing Random Forest-based Grid Search Cross Validation (RF GSCV) for hyperparameter tuning, aimed at enhancing classification models to estimating type 2 diabetes (T2DM). The starting focus of this research is to improve the SOTA accuracy of the models and ensure their adaptability across diverse datasets. A dataset consisting of 520 individuals, characterized by various diabetic symptoms, was used to predict the likelihood of developing diabetes, considering both positive and negative probabilities. Optimal parameters were applied to three classification models—Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, and Extra Trees (ET)—to predict diabetes. The models is validated using 10-crossvalidation, with the Extra Trees model achieving the highest classification accuracy of 97.60%.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Traditional and Ensemble Learning Models for Network Security System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: In this paper use CIC-IDS2017 dataset to illustrate a comparative analysis of traditional and proposed models for intrusion detection in network security systems. The comparison includes DT, RF, ET and XGBoost classifiers. Normalize class, SMOTE Data preprocessing to compensate for missing values and of imbalance classes From the results of evaluation metrics, we conclude that proposed methods show a significant improvement on its model performances in detecting network intrusions as compared to traditional models XGboost specifically this work. Out of all the algorithms, the accuracy for XGBoost stands out, as it is mostly known to cater to complex attack patterns. The results indicate that ensemble base techniques offer the best solutions which can prove to be both effective and efficient as an intrusion detection systems for current network technologies.

articleTitle: A Survey on Hand Gesture Sign Language Recognition with Arduino Leonardo
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: This study examined the research on the project investigates the integration of sign language into a hand gesture recognition system that relies on vision. the review's findings indicate that the field of The study of hand gesture recognition using eyesight is dynamic, with several investigations carried out and dozens of articles published yearly in journals and conference proceedings. Three crucial elements of the vision-based hand gesture recognition system, notably hand gesture representation, were the focus of the majority of these studies.deep learning methods with an Arduino Leonardo for hand gesture recognition. An accelerometer sensor on the Arduino Leonardo records dynamic hand movement data. After being sent to a computer, this sensor data is processed by a deep learning model that has been trained to identify particular motions. I practice word-by-word modeling rather than two-word, two-line training.

articleTitle: Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna for 5G,6G, and mm Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The proposed high-gain rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) is optimized for X, K, and Ka bands with a defective ground structure (DGS) and microstrip feed, enhancing impedance matching, current distribution, and bandwidth. A defective ground structure (DGS) featuring strategically placed circular and rectangular cuts, improves impedance matching, controls current distribution, and enhances bandwidth. It contributes to these enhancements by optimizing power transfer. the operating frequencies of 18.3GHz, 27.2GHz, and 35GHz, and covering a bandwidth of 12.5-21.42GHz its S11=44.2dB, 25.1-29.8GHz its S11=17.2dB and 31.4-36.6GHz its S11=24.2dB, where good impedance matching is evident. It covers bandwidths of 48.47%, 17.27%, and 14.85% respectively. Gain of 7.8 dB, 8.22 dB, and 8.12 dB. The radiation efficiency was more than 94.82%,96.52%, and 98.81 % respectively, it is ideal for applications like satellite communications, radar, and high-frequency wireless systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing Security in Logic-Locked Systems Through UART-Based Key Authentication
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The security of integrated circuits is crucial due to their wide range of applications in modern gadgets. An unauthorized access (i.e., third-party access) or a security breach in the logic-locked system can pose a great threat to user privacy, thus leading to data theft and misusing the user data. Several logic locking methods have been proposed, but with the advancements of technology, the latest attack techniques can easily crack those existing locking techniques. Thus, in this research paper we have proposed a sensor-based methodology to detect the unauthorized access with microswitch and UART. In a globalized world where the security of logic-locked systems is really important, this paper empathizes with UART-based mechanisms as a practical solution. By focusing on the existing logic locking methodologies, this paper contributes to the ongoing security efforts for a secured logic locked system.

articleTitle: Generative Artificial Intelligence Based Biomedical Applications for Pharmaceutical Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The quick advancement in AI has led to the development of refined large language models (LLM). While LLM is a specific type of generative AI focused on generative text generative AI is a broader category encompassing various AI systems that can generate new content including texts, images, music, and more generation models. Generative AI is transforming various fields, like education, finance, marketing, fashion, gaming, medical area or healthcare. Generative AI finds its applications in improving drug discovery, biomedical instrument design, and healthcare delivery within the pharmaceutical industry. In this study, we aim to find generative artificial intelligence-based biomedical applications for the pharmaceutical industry.

articleTitle: Wearable Temperature Detection System for Personalised Health Tracking
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The health of a human being is indicated by various vitals like heart rate, blood pressure, respiration rate, and body temperature, to name a few. An accurate measure of temperature is an essential parameter while monitoring temperature in critical conditions, especially for frontline workers, where continuous temperature measurement is of prime importance. This work analyses temperature sensors and explores various testing methods for response time and methods to improve the parameters. A customised PCB and temperature sensors were designed, fabricated, and tested. A custom-made Android app was also developed and tested to visualise the data from the sensors. The test results showed that the system developed has a quick response time of 4 to 6 seconds for a temperature change of 65°C and complies with military standards set by DRDO.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of One-Hot Encoding vs Response Coding in Context of Social Media Text Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Most of the content on various social media platforms has enormous textual data. Before being used in machine learning models, this textual data must be transformed into numerical formats using feature extraction and feature engineering techniques to improve classification accuracy. Numerous methods, including Label Encoding, Response Coding, One-hot Encoding, and Binary Encoding, are available for converting textual input into numerical values, and these methods are effective in handling massive amounts of textual data. This study investigates how these methods can be applied to social media reviews and comments to establish the most effective encoding technique for classification machine learning models that recognize sentiment polarity. We selected a social media dataset with 44,955 tweets for our work and divided it into train, test, and cross-validation. Experimental results show that One-hot encoding performed the best with Logistic regression, whereas Response coding was less efficient.

articleTitle: TurfIt: An Instant Turf Booking Application
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: As sports grow in popularity need for effective online turf booking applications has also increased. Although some existing applications are faced with numerous challenges such as; restrictions on access, ineffectiveness in scheduling, and over-bookings, leading to frustrations and operational problems. This paper focuses on those problems by the presentation of an online turf booking application to streamline the booking process. The solution offers real-time updates, automatic payment, and safe transactions based on QR code. The more user-friendly the application is, the more efficient it will be. Firebase would be used for real-time data synchronization and the responsiveness of React interface ensures the smooth and conflict-free bookings. This solution would lead to increasing customer satisfaction as well as increasing the booking rates and effective utilization of sports facilities.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Low-Cost IoT-Based Smart Agricultural System Using ESP32 and LoRa Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a low-cost IoT-based smart agricultural system utilizing the ESP32 microcontroller and LoRa technology. The system integrates multiple sensors, including those for soil moisture, temperature, and humidity, to monitor essential environmental parameters. It also supports real-time image capture for crop assessment using the ESP32-CAM module. Data collected by the sensors is processed by the ESP32 and transmitted wirelessly via LoRa to a central gateway, which connects to the cloud for storage and analysis. This architecture provides flexibility and long-range communication, making it suitable for large agricultural fields. An intuitive dashboard enables farmers to visualize real-time data and control actuators remotely, facilitating automated irrigation and other field operations. The proposed system emphasizes affordability, scalability, and ease of replication, offering a practical solution for enhancing productivity and sustainability in agriculture.

articleTitle: Image Recognition for Wildlife Conservation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: This study adopts an empirical approach to evaluate the efficacy of image processing methods in conservation efforts for animals. The initial phase involves the collection of data from various sources within the natural ecosystem, including images captured through camera traps, drones, and other monitoring devices. This comprehensive and diverse dataset is then processed using advanced Image Processing Tools. A key strength of this methodology lies in its use of Machine Learning algorithms, particularly YOLO v8 (You Only Look Once) and Support Vector Machines (SVMs). These techniques are suitable for wildlife conservation because of their capacity to analyze complex visual data and detect patterns indicative of species presence, behavior, and habitat conditions. The paper outlines the application of YOLO v8 and SVMs to the collected image data, enabling accurate identification, real-time detection, and classification of wildlife species. This capability is essential for monitoring populations, tracking movements, and identifying potential threats, thus facilitating timely conservation actions. Furthermore, the research extends its evaluation by comparing the results of the Machine Learning approach with traditional ecological survey methods, offering a comprehensive assessment of the effectiveness of image processing in wildlife conservation.

articleTitle: A Multi-Algorithm Stacking Approach to Lung Cancer Detection with SVM, GBM, Naive Bayes, Decision Tree, and Random Forest Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
