abstract: Lung health is one of the most minor medical issues globally because of its low mortality rate and high chance of early detection. The model presented here is a multi-model design that uses vector machines, gradient boosting machines, random forests, decision trees, and naive non-Bayesian machine learning techniques to worsen lung cancer diagnosis. This method is avoided for the lung cancer dataset from Kaggle, and a fragmented model is used to undermine the model's performance. It is seen that among the combinations, the stacked model and SVM have the highest accuracy of 0.95, followed by GBM with 0.944, random forest with 0.944, decision tree with 0.93, and naive Bayes with 0.87. The assembly model combines the outputs of various distributions to make the hull robust and accurate. This study emphasizes the potential of using machine learning to enhance self-treatment outcomes for cancer patients and, therefore, calls for early diagnosis to reduce mortality rates.

articleTitle: Synergy of AI and PMBLDC Motors: Enhancing Efficiency in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are showing a great deal of interest in Permanent Magnet Brushless Direct Current (PMBLDC) motors due to the growing need for environmentally friendly transportation options. The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) like Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC) in the control and management of PMBLDC motors is revolutionizing the performance and efficiency of EVs. This paper explores the multifaceted applications of AI in optimizing PMBLDC motor operations, including advanced motor control techniques and adaptive performance tuning. AI enhances torque response, minimizes energy consumption, and extends motor lifespan. The synergy between AI and PMBLDC motors not only improves the driving experience but also contributes to the overall sustainability of electric transportation. This study highlights the transformative potential of AI in achieving higher efficiency and reliability in PMBLDC motor applications, paving the way for the future of electric mobility.

articleTitle: Lung and Colon Cancer Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Lung cancer is a dangerous illness affecting humans. The kind and location of the cancer will mostly determine the course of medical therapy. Detecting cancer cells at the earliest possible stage has the potential to save a great number of irreplaceable human lives. Developing an automated method is crucial for early cancer detection. Despite various methods offered by scholars, prediction accuracy has always been a difficulty. To address this challenge, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) - based Lung and Colon Cancer classification is presented in this paper. The dataset was gathered from Kaggle to train and test the network. The data is pre-processed to be suitable for the CNN model. The performance of the customized CNN model is evaluated in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and f1-score, The proposed model is suitable for assisting doctors in classifying Lung and Colon Cancer.

articleTitle: Robust Intrusion Detection System to Protect Cloud Services
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Cloud data centers are normally designed to handle dynamic work load and any type of large scale operation. But some of the characteristics of the datacenters make them vulnerable to Distributed Denial of Service attacks. An attack which involves data centers as target not only affect that center but also all the services hosted within that data center. Service availability will be severely affected by this attack. For a robust network defense mechanism, it is critical to detect and classify these attacks. The era that exists today is of Generative Artificial Intelligence and other technologies, which is very helpful to complete various tasks. Which can also be used for the effective detection of Distributed Denial of Service attack. To detect these attacks this project, propose a novel approach using BERT model. Transformer based architectures like BERT can be used to analyze various attack scenarios and predict potential attacks even it can specify the type of the attack. BERT is fine-tuned using a dataset containing both normal and Denial of Service attack from that the model can learn the subtle patterns which is helpful in distinguishing the types of these attack. In this project we compared the results with traditional models and BERT. From that we can see how BERT performs very well in the detection. Real time detection will provide a solution to overcome these attacks and provide a more robust defense against Distributed Denial of Service attacks.

articleTitle: Building Resilient CICD Pipelines: A DevOps Security-First Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment are now integrated in automated systems that enhance code stability, and accelerate the deployment process as well as improving monitoring of the whole system in the software development field. This document deals with setting up of a strong CI/CD process involving AWS cloud services and DevOps. The infrastructure is built with the help of Terraform which ensures the scalability and repeatability applying the Infrastructure as Code (IaC) approach. A safe Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) is designed consisting of public and private subnets, load balancing for traffic distribution, and CloudFront CDN to improve geographical distribution. Jenkins is used in CI process to perform disk analysis, OWASP and Trivy vulnerability scanning, and making Docker images. The CD phase use ArgoCD for updates on Kubernetes and integrates Monitoring and observability using Prometheus and Grafana. Notifications are produced to JIRA and email communication for improvement. With the help of the offered cloud services and DevOps tool it is possible to consolidate the SDLC and bring effects in code safety, testing and utilization. This document also provides an overview of methods, instruments, and outcomes, demonstrating how the CI/CD automation influences the development and operation positively.

articleTitle: AI Based Targeting and Tracking System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: This paper introduces an AI-driven tracking and targeting system poised to revolutionize precision across surveil- lance, defense, and tracking. Traditional systems often struggle with dynamic environments and accuracy optimization. Lever- aging AI, our system integrates advanced computer vision and deep neural networks for real-time object detection and tracking. Through machine learning, the system adapts to evolving scenarios, progressively enhancing tracking performance. Additionally, prevention of casualties with respect of loss of life, this model acts as a firewall from possible threats. This AI-based system signifies a significant advancement, promising heightened precision and efficiency across diverse applications. Its integration of cutting- edge technologies positions it at the forefront of tracking and targeting systems, marking a noteworthy contribution to the field.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Algorithms for Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) Navigation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) play an extremely important role in the fields of oceanography, marine science and underwater infrastructure assessment. Of course, underwater navigation isn't easy either due to varying ocean currents, limited vision, and there's no GPS. This article uses machine learning techniques to describe how AUV navigation can be improved in underwater environments with unknown environment, then enable more reliable decision making and real time obstacle avoidance. This thesis investigates many ML approaches for route planning, sensor data fusion, and obstacle detection including supervised, unsupervised learning and reinforcement learning. With great significance, reinforcement learning algorithms can optimize trial and error learning based navigation techniques to be adapted to novel situations. Additionally, deep leaning algorithms combined with data from sensors such as sonar and cameras are able to enable precise underwater landscape perception and mapping. We apply these algorithms to virtual and physical AUV missions and demonstrate that they result in significant increases in navigation precision, energy efficiency, and mission time. This research's careful consideration of the potential of machine learning for transforming AUV navigation makes more intelligent and autonomous underwater operations possible in many marine sectors.

articleTitle: Optimized Hybrid Deep Learning Approach for Detecting DoS Attacks Using Feature Selection in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The rapid growth of smart cities, healthcare monitoring, and environmental sensing relies heavily on the real-time data processing capabilities of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). However, these networks face significant security challenges, particularly from malicious activities like Denial of Service(DoS) attacks, which can disrupt critical operations. A hybrid intrusion detection model that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Deep Neural Networks (DNN) to improve the detection of such threats has been proposed. The preprocessing phase includes the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) which mitigates class imbalances ensuring robust performance across diverse attack scenarios. The model incorporates advanced feature selection techniques including SelectKBest and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) to identify the most critical features for enhanced detection accuracy. The CNN component effectively captures local traffic patterns, which are then refined by the DNN for accurate classification. This hybrid model's effectiveness in detecting diverse DoS attack scenarios is evaluated using WSN-DS dataset, ensuring robust security for WSNs. By achieving an impressive 98% detection accuracy, this hybrid model proves to be effective in intrusion detection. Its applications can significantly strengthen the security and reliability of WSNs, ensuring uninterrupted operations in key sectors such as smart cities, healthcare, and environmental monitoring.

articleTitle: Leveraging IoT and AI in Precision Agriculture for Efficient Water Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Where water is limited the challenge of getting the best management of the resource become a major issue in farming. In this study, therefore, we focus on the following question: What role may AI and the IoT play in precision agriculture towards enhancing sustainability through the conservation of water resources? IoT devices that can provide information on the environmental conditions include; sensors for moisture level in the soil, and weather systems. To such data artificial intelligence algorithms are applied to automate the process of irrigation, determine possible water consumption and avoid excess. Real-time and historical data can also be evaluated using machine learning approaches of the system. From this it is then able to predict when crops will need water and then align their irrigation times from this information. Moreover, the analytic model using AI may find potential issues with irrigation and present mitigating steps. Juxtaposing IoT and AI, it is revealed in this research how the two technologies can improve water management decisionmaking with the aim of minimizing water depletion as well as over-irrigation. Integrated soil nutrients management and conservation agriculture are recommended and the overall atmospheric water scarce zone sustainable agricultural productivity is enhanced by the proposed framework while increasing water productivity. The study reveals that it is possible to steer the future of water management through the interconnection of IoT and AI in precision agriculture. It may therefore result in higher production, efficiency in resource utilization and ultimate sustainability.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised Learning: The Core of Next-Gen Machine Learning and a Paradigm Shift in AI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) commands advance tutoring models beyond the need of wide labeled data, making it scarce for fields with restricted annotated resources, like computer vision, NLP, remote sensing, and imaging in the field of medicals. By manipulating pseudo-labels from pretext tasks, SSL methods have drawn attention for their advancements like image classification and even object detection. This study aims to draw light on contrastive SSL, which acquires the knowledge robustly, invariant features with data transformations, refining model resilience to adversarial perturbations and labeled noises. The Self-Supervised Semi-Supervised Learning (SSL) framework which accumulates SSL with Semi-Supervised techniques, is known for its effectiveness through high-performance models with small labeled Implementations in remote sensing and medical imaging SSL's verbalities and abstraction across domains. This study scrutinizes SSL strategies, examines performance benchmarks, and recognizes future research directions for applicability. upgrading robustness and SSL promises well-regulated and multi-skilled learning with nominal labeled data required.

articleTitle: Improving Accuracy of Object Detection in Autonomous Drones with Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Increasing use of autonomous drones in such areas as agriculture, disaster response and surveillance means that an effective and precise method of object recognition is becoming more important. In this study, we use Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to bring additional precision to autonomous drone object detecting systems. While conventional machine learning approaches fail miserably in having complicated contexts and real time processing, CNN have sucessfully handles visual identification task. Based on state of the art methods being data augmentation and transfer learning, plus being real time with data augmentation of the raw data on the edge processor, this research introduces a convolutional neural network (CNN) model which has been fine-tuned and can be used for drones. The model is trained and tested on a big dataset of aerial photos acquired by drones. The item classification on this dataset varies from lighting conditions, to weather variables, etc. A considerable increase in the object detection accuracy is found from experimental findings in reducing false positives and improving resilience in dynamic contexts. Furthermore, the suggested model allows for detection with little latency, making it a good model for drones that must be deployed in real-time. Not only does this work contribute to bolstering rapidly growing autonomous drone navigation, it has great promise in environmental monitoring, SAR, and precision agriculture, and other applications. The components of the models are being researched on how scalable they are and how do they scale up on hardware that has limited resources.

articleTitle: AI in Medical Imaging: Enhancing Diagnostic Accuracy with Deep Convolutional Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The past has witnessed a time of astounding developments in AI, particularly notable deep convolutional networks, which has greatly facilitated medical imaging by opening up previously unattainable doors for both precision and effectiveness of diagnoses. This study is an investigation into how deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) might be applied (using MRI, CT, and X-ray as examples) to medical imaging for the purposes of improving accuracy, consistency, and practicability of diagnostic procedures. Through automated feature extraction and categorization, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) enable earlier, and more accurate, detection of illnesses such as cancer, cardiovascular disease and neurological problems by detecting minor deviations that humans may miss. Here we evaluate the accuracy, sensitivity, and computing efficiency of several convolutional network (CNN) designs. ResNet and UNet are these architectures. The results indicate that CNN based models provide better performance compared to conventional diagnostic approaches with a substantial diminution in both false positives and false negatives. The article also covers combining CNNs with others AI methods such as transfer learning, ensemble methods, etc. to further improve diagnostic results. Although the encouraging outcomes, data protection, interpretability, and clinical acceptance continue to be obstacles. This study shows how AI driven technology can revolutionize medical imaging to enhance patient outcomes as well as tailored healthcare solutions.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Web Analysis of Automobile Websites: Performance, SEO, and Accessibility Insights
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The current research work proposes a difficultydriven comparison of three most visited automobile websites namely the Automobile Site1, Automobile Site2, Automobile Site3 on parameters including performance, Search engine optimization (SEO), accessibility and traffic. The research involves tool such as Yellow Labs, Google Page Speed Insight and Semrush with regard to the website's weight, loading time, user's interactions and search engine optimization. The findings reveal distinct strengths across the sites: From the three Automobile Site1 is the most optimized and accessibly friendly site, the factors of search engine friendliness is as follows. Looking at the traffic and users of Automobile Site2, it comfortably outclasses the other sites in terms of page views as well as the audience loyalty. At the same time, Automobile Site3 has relatively low first load time which indicates fast website browsing while it is still relatively weak in terms of its SEO and the usability of the site has to be improved in terms of theoretical potential. In conclusion, the realized comparison exposes the strengths and weaknesses of each site and is informative to future developments of the sites with an aim at better user interaction levels and competitive advantage.

articleTitle: A Hybrid CNN-LSTM Model for Enhanced Intrusion Detection in Internet of Things Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The exponential expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) has precipitated a concerning increase in advanced cyber-attacks, posing significant problems for the protection of these networked systems. Traditional Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) frequently encounter difficulties in handling the complexity and high-dimensional characteristics of IoT traffic, especially in situations involving various attack vectors. To mitigate these restrictions, we present a hybrid deep learning model that amalgamates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. By integrating the advantages of various architectures, the model proficiently identifies spatial patterns using CNNs and temporal dependencies through LSTMs, facilitating precise traffic classification. Utilizing the NF-BoT-IoT dataset, our methodology exhibited remarkable efficacy, attaining an accuracy of 99.52% and an F1-score of 0.9923 in binary classification, with an accuracy of 98.89% in multi-class classification across several attack categories. These findings highlight the model's resilience and its capability as a real-time intrusion detection system, facilitating improved security in IoT networks across diverse settings.

articleTitle: Multiple Slip Influence on Maxwell Fluid Flow Around a Porous Vertical Cone with Addition of Nanofluid Particles: MHD and Convective Boundary Condition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: When Brownian motion is present in a non-Newtonian Maxwell-nanofluid flowing through a vertical cone filled with porous material, the authors used numerical solutions to probe the mixed impacts of unique slip effects, thermal radiation, mass transfer, and heat change characteristics. This was done in order to find out the mixed influences of Brownian motion. They discovered that flow of a non-Newtonian Maxwell-nanofluid influenced these characteristics. When the researchers analyzed the process that happens when a vertical cone becomes immerse in a porous condition, they took into account concentration slip boundary conditions, velocity, convective boundary conditions, heat and mass change, thermophoresis, and a magnetic field. A model compose of a collection of nonlinear governing partial differential equation (PDE) subject to boundary condition is use to offer a quantitative description of the underlying physical state. The Keller box method is use to solve differential equation with well-defined boundary condition numerically. The exact outcomes will be displayed in the form of a graph to demonstrate how the temperature, concentration, and speed are affected by changes in the controlling factors. According to this point of view, the presence of these components has a substantial effect on several technical applications, such as the production of polymers, metal layers, paper sheets, nuclear reactor cores, and sectors related to biotechnology. The computational findings are backed up by a comparison of individual instances from the current research to those from earlier investigations, which reveal a high level of concordance among the both sets of data. Because of this, we are able to go on with the computational analysis that is required for this assignment.

articleTitle: Spectrum Sensing Techniques in Cognitive Radio Based Wireless Regional Area Network: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: As wireless communication technology has advanced, so too has the need for wireless gadgets. It is extremely necessary for spectrum to enable these wireless devices because it is the foundation of wireless communication. Cognitive Radio (CR) uses spectrum sensing to identify the available bandwidth. Other cognitive radio functions can be achieved after spectrum sensing is established. Therefore, the primary prerequisite for cognitive radio is effective spectrum sensing. This paper discusses spectrum sensing methods and issues. The framework of cognitive radio is summarized based on research. This work discusses collaborative spectrum detection and the ways it is classified. We also looked into the IEEE standards' spectral scanning techniques.

articleTitle: Eye-Gaze Controlled Virtual Keyboard Using Blink Detection for Accessible Hands-Free Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The inability to interact with traditional input devices like keyboards poses significant challenges for individuals with motor impairments. Existing assistive technologies often rely on cumbersome and expensive hardware solutions, which are not accessible to everyone. This paper addresses the problem by presenting an affordable and accessible gaze-controlled virtual keyboard that uses only a standard webcam. The project utilizes computer vision algorithms, specifically dlib's face detection and shape prediction, to detect facial landmarks and calculate the Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR), which enables accurate eye-blink detection. The system is designed to dynamically highlight letter groups on a virtual keyboard, allowing users to select keys through a series of eye blinks. The keyboard switches between letter groups and individual letters, facilitating text entry without requiring physical input. The proposed solution demonstrates how computer vision techniques can be used to enhance accessibility and independence for users with severe motor disabilities by providing a practical and user-friendly interface.

articleTitle: Federated Learning in Healthcare: A Privacy-Preserving Approach to Predictive Analytics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Technology such as machine learning in healthcare has pushed privacy concerns to the point that the handling of sensitive patient data has become paramount. In the context of FL, predictive analytics without data sharing between institutions can be performed through the process. Next, we explore the application of FL in healthcare in order to maintain data privacy while obtaining robust predictive models. FL utilizes aggregated decentralized data from multiple healthcare providers to reduce the chance of data breaches and continue to be compliant with rigorous regulatory frameworks, like HIPAA and GDPR, while doing so. In this work, we evaluate the model performance of FL models in predicting different types of health outcomes in comparison with traditional centralized models. We show that FL can achieve similar predictive accuracy while maintaining data privacy, which makes the choice of FL as a viable alternative to privacy sensitive healthcare environments. Second, applying FL is very challenging: there are communication overhead, data heterogeneity, and security risks. This study also considers ways to minimize these challenges. The results demonstrate the promise of Federated Learning as an innovative paradigm for applying predictive analytics in healthcare, indicative of a robust shift toward more secure, efficient and privacy preserving healthcare systems.

articleTitle: Image Tampering Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: This paper proposes an image forgery detection technique combining the use of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Error Level Analysis (ELA) for efficiently distinguishing tampered images from those that are original. ELA identifies potential regions of manipulation based on the discrepancy of the compression artifacts, whereas the VGG16based CNN classifier distinguishes between original and tampered images. The proposed model was assessed using the CASIA2 dataset, thus illustrating its effectiveness in accurately classifying images. This research contributes to the field of digital forensics, providing an advanced method for ensuring the integrity and authenticity of digital content, which is crucial for security and verification in various applications.

articleTitle: Detecting Cyber Threat Using Gen-AI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: As we stand in the era of 6G, the ultra-fast and low-latency connectivity opens up numerous possibilities for innovation, across various sectors. These advancements bring more sophisticated cyber threats. The complexity and scale of 6G networks demand innovative approaches to cybersecurity, and this is where generative AI (GenAI)can play a transformative role. Traditional cybersecurity measures such as signature-based detection and heuristic analysis, have served us well in the past. The deep learning models like BERT have numerous in cyber threat detection, the need for efficient detection methods is critical because of more frequent and complex threats, With differential privacy with embedding perturbation technique(DPEP). The Bert model provides a cutting-edge architecture to detect threats with high precision. Through the experiments held on the Edge-IIoT set cybersecurity dataset, Bert has achieved 91.2% accuracy. Thus, Bert might be an optimal solution for real-time threat detection, especially for deploying resource-constrained loT environments.

articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning to Predict Obesity Trends: Insights from Lifestyle and Biometric Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: This is increasingly important as global obesity rates continue to rise: the causes need to be understood, and the ability to predict trends determined. In this study, we use machine learning techniques to predict obesity trends given lifestyle and biometric data from a large obesity dataset. Our methodology starts with data preprocessing that includes transforming categorical variables into numerical variables and standardizes the numerical variables into such a form so that machine learning algos can work with them properly. Supervised machine learning models, such as tree based methods, neural networks and various ensemble techniques are applied, and evaluated. For determining the most effective predictive approach, these models are evaluated by several performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score; the best model is chosen based on these metrics. In addition, the study includes explainable AI technique (SHAP—SHapley Additive exPlanations; LIME—Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations) to make the results more interpretable. The results from these methods provide insight into how different lifestyle and biometric factors contribute to the prediction of obesity; such as physical activity, diet patterns, and body mass index. The results from this work demonstrate not only how machine learning can improve prediction accuracy but also how these methods can provide actionable insights into the many contributing factors to obesity.

articleTitle: Harnessing the Power of AI With Deep Learning: Innovations and Implications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The rapid advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning have revolutionized various sectors, enabling unprecedented levels of innovation and efficiency. This paper delves into the transformative impact of deep learning across multiple domains, highlighting key innovations and their broader implications. By examining cutting-edge applications in healthcare, finance, autonomous systems, and natural language processing, the study elucidates how deep learning models, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs), are pushing the boundaries of what's possible. Moreover, the paper explores the integration of deep learning with emerging technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), edge computing, and quantum computing, underscoring the synergistic potential of these combinations. The role of deep learning in predictive analytics and personalized solutions is discussed, showcasing its ability to enhance decision-making processes and improve user experiences. Furthermore, the paper discusses the ethical considerations, challenges, and future prospects associated with the widespread adoption of deep learning technologies. The insights provided aim to foster a deeper understanding of how harnessing AI with deep learning can drive progress while addressing critical societal and technological issues.

articleTitle: A Novel Deep Learning Model Based Lung Cancer Detection of Histopathological Images
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Lung cancer is still one of the world's top causes of death, and increasing survival rates require early identification. Biopsied tissue must be histopathologically analyzed for diagnosis; however, manual inspection can be laborious and error-prone, increasing the possibility of a mistake and inappropriate therapy. This study examines how well several deep learning models—EfficientNetB0, ResNet50, VGG19, VGG16, and InceptionV3—classify lung tissue into three categories: benign, malignant, and normal. InceptionV3 (81%), VGG19 (94%), VGG16 (90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), ResNet50 (95<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), and the EfficientNetB0 model (98<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) all had the highest accuracy. Through highly accurate cancer categorization automation, these models promise to improve diagnostic efficiency, reduce pathologists' workload, and minimize errors. Developing dependable computer-aided diagnostic systems is supported by the comparative assessment of various architectures, which guarantees optimal performance. To improve patient outcomes, this work offers insightful information for future developments in deep learning systems for lung cancer detection.

articleTitle: End-User-Centric Cloud Security: An Integrated Approach for File Encryption and Decryption with Blowfish and AWS
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: With the growing trend of cloud computing, the necessity for secure data storage arises as traditional security measures fail with different types of new emerging cyber threats. The paper introduces a file storage system that maintains secure data confidentiality and integrity in the cloud environment using Blowfish encryption. File upload will now allow a user to encrypt and store files for decryption purposes only by authorized users with their encryption keys. Key functionalities will include strong authentication of users, file encryption, and key management according to secure management-all housed within a cloud infrastructure-AWS. This also serves to aid in multiple host systems access, hence scalable and reliable.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity With Machine Learning: Implementing AI Algorithms for Intrusion Prevention, Advanced Data Protection, and Real-Time Threat Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: In an era where cyber attacks are getting increasingly complex, the incorporation of machine learning (ML) algorithms into cybersecurity processes has emerged as a crucial technique for boosting protection against potential intrusions and data breaches. For the purpose of preventing intrusions, providing superior data protection, and conducting real-time threat analysis, this research investigates the application of machine learning approaches that are driven by artificial intelligence. Organizations are able to increase their preventative defenses against cyber attacks by utilizing algorithms that are capable of analyzing massive volumes of data and identifying patterns that are indicative of harmful behavior. Several machine learning (ML) approaches, including supervised and unsupervised learning, anomaly detection, and neural networks, are investigated in this study. The purpose of the study is to demonstrate the usefulness of these approaches in identifying and responding to a wide range of security concerns. In addition to this, the research investigates the significance of continual learning and adaptation in machine learning models, which enables these models to develop alongside developments in new threats. The findings highlight the potential for machine learning to change cybersecurity frameworks by delivering speedy and automatic reactions to incidents. This would lead to the protection of sensitive information and an overall improvement in the system's resilience. In the end, this research highlights the importance of implementing tactics that are based on artificial intelligence in order to meet the intricacies of modern cyber threats and maintain robust security in a world that is becoming increasingly digital.

articleTitle: Loan Prediction Analysis Using Innumerable Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Internet loan fraud has emerged as a significant challenge in the financial industry, causing substantial economic losses and undermining trust in digital lending platforms. Applicants’ information includes income, level of education, employment status, loan amount, and credit histories, among other relevant variable information. Data preparation should start with the essential data pre-processing tasks: imputation of missing values for variables, encoding categorical values, and normalizing of numerical features. The dataset is divided between training and testing subsets when evaluating the model. The XG-Boost classifier is utilized to predict loan approvals, with its performance gauged by metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. Hyperparameter tuning is used to improve model performance. Results suggest that the XG-Boost classifier provides high accuracy for loan approval predictions. Also, the feature importance analysis suggests key factors that have a strong influence on the model's decisions, showing the potential of the algorithm in helping financial institutions make better decisions. This study shows the scalability and effectiveness of XGBoost for practical credit risk prediction tasks.

articleTitle: Harnessing Tech Innovations for Diversified Multigenerational Work Force and Work Life Balance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: This research aims to examine how technologically innovative breakthroughs may help a multigenerational heterogeneous workforce to maintain a good work and life balance. We investigate how technology can be used to strategically raise up the rate of participation and align with the particular needs of different age groups. The research findings show how AI powered personal learning, collaborative digital communication tools and flexible remote working solutions promote a healthy and mature culture in the workplace. The findings explain how key it is to utilize technology in a refined manner such that all workers can thrive and maintain a sustainable balance between their work and home life.

articleTitle: Efficient Load Balancing in Software Defined Networks Using Unsupervised Meta-Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: New technologies, such as cloud computing and big data, make traditional network management more difficult, while the network's user base continues to expand. Consequently, changes to the traditional network architecture are required. To address this issue and enhance network management compliance, a new idea called software-defined network (SDN) has been proposed. Due to limited network resources and to satisfy the criteria of quality of service, it is necessary to address numerous difficulties, one of which is load balancing (LB), which distributes data traffic among several resources to maximize their efficiency and reliability. The local information of a network is used to design LB in a typical network. Consequently, it is not very accurate. Still, software-defined network (SDN) controllers can see the network from anywhere in the world and make better LB. We provide a set of unsupervised meta- RL algorithms to build smart optimization architecture for SDN LB.

articleTitle: Accessing Deep Learning Techniques for Commodity Price Prediction: A Comparative Assessment Across Energy, Precious Metal, and Agricultural Futures
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: This study performs an in-depth comparison of deep learning approaches - CNN, LSTM, GRU, and their bidirectional variants (BiLSTM and BiGRU) - to anticipate commodity futures prices, particularly in the crude oil, gold, and corn markets. The approach used in our study combines fundamental and technical factors with thorough variable selection to establish the most effective predictors. The Grid Search Cross-Validation approach is employed for optimizing the hyperparameters of deep learning architectures. The efficacy of applied models is evaluated using common evaluation indicators: Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Coefficient of Determination(R2), and Adjusted R2. The results presented enhance the existing research on AI applications in financial markets, providing recommendations for the development of more precise forecasting techniques for researchers.

articleTitle: Collating Random Forest Classifier and Artificial Neural Networks for the Risk Detection of Maternal Health
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: This paper compares the performance of ANN models to Random Forests on benchmarking a test dataset against the risk levels of maternal health as low, mid, or high. The features considered are clinical features, namely age, blood pressure, and heart rate. The dataset was imbalanced and needed adapting the ANN architecture by fitting class weights and dropout regularization. The best test accuracy obtained in this fashion was 73%. As the ANN had learned many of the complex data patterns in the dataset, it was, however, still limited by the moderate size and skewness of the dataset. The Random Forest model with grid search produced a much better accuracy of 85.71% compared with ANN, thereby suggesting relatively high generalization across all the classes for better minority risk level classes. An ensemble approach of the Random Forest method appears to better serve toward high accuracy along with interpretability for clinical decision support in maternal health risk assessment.

articleTitle: Tracing Performance Trends of Self-Help Groups Across India: A Social Computing Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Self Help Groups (SHGs) are voluntary associations of economically disadvantaged individuals, primarily rural women in India, who come together to overcome poverty and address community issues through self-reliance and collective action. This paper endeavors to scrutinize the impacts of savings and loan disbursement on the Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) of banks concerning SHGs. The study seeks to identify the performance of SHGs in India over time, using appropriate social computing analytical methods, specifically during 2007–08 to 2022–23 across six regions of India, namely, central, eastern, northeastern, northern, southern, and western India. Initially summary statistics on the chosen variables have been calculated. For the purpose of analysis, panel data regression analyses have been used, prior to which test for stationarity of the variables of interest have been conducted and test for co-integration have been performed. Hausman test has been used to choose between random effects and fixed effects models. All variables have been found to be stationary at first difference and the presence of cointegration has been supported. Hausman test gave evidence in favour of random effects model. The analysis reveals that NPAs are the most volatile variable, followed by loan disbursement and savings per SHG. Interestingly, the study concludes that loan disbursement and savings have a detrimental effect on NPA growth concerning SHGs. There is a need for financial institutions to develop effective mechanisms for managing the credit risk associated with lending to SHGs, while also supporting their efforts to improve their economic situation.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Mental Health Assessment using Emotion Detection for Real-Time Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: This paper is an AI-driven mental health assessment tailored to each patient's distinct emotional needs, addressing the global mental health crisis. Using advanced machine learning and natural language processing, it aims to deliver personalized guidance for psychological and physical wellness activities, along with tools for tracking individual progress. The papers employ exploratory case studies and knowledge discovery techniques to evaluate the effectiveness of these interventions. Data mining methods reveal hidden patterns within mental health datasets, with the potential to reshape therapeutic paradigms. Expected outcomes include enhanced accessibility to mental health resources, early intervention, personalized progress monitoring, improved quality of life, and reduced stigma. By integrating sophisticated data processing, machine learning, and empathetic user interaction, it operates by redefining mental health support. The system's architecture is designed to promote both emotional and cognitive well-being, fostering positive change in mental health care delivery.

articleTitle: The Comprehensive Review of Different Categories, Applications, and Methods Used In Healthcare Recommender System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Nowadays, in the digital world, healthcare stands out as one of the most prominent domains in the health field. A healthcare system (HS) is essential for studying a vast quantity of patient records, aiding in deriving insights and assisting in the prediction of diseases. The Healthcare Recommendation System (HRS) is emerging as a vital platform for medical services. This review article provides a comprehensive analysis of existing recommendation methods, including content-based, collaborative, hybrid, etc. The main focus of the article is to offer a review of Recommender Systems (RS) in healthcare. It delves into distinct methods used for healthcare RSs, such as clustering-based, regression, and classification-based methods like CNN, SVD, etc. Existing classification-based HRS methods have achieved the maximum accuracy rate compared to other methods.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of IoT Prototypes: Leveraging Test-Beds for Performance Assessment and Innovation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: When you mention the Internet of things (IoT), connected devices and systems can be made seamless. Whilst creating and prototyping IoTs are oftentimes necessary, design, testing and evaluating IoT prototypes require robust frameworks and methodologies to achieve reliable performance and innovation. In this paper, test beds as controlled environments for performance assessment of IoT prototypes are discussed and these tested in terms of design and evaluation. Of importance are test-beds as they aid in simulating real world conditions to do iterative improvements, and foster innovation in IoT solutions. It presents some key methodologies for developing IoT prototypes, underlines the role of test beds in the validation process, and reports about evaluation of some case studies demonstrating the impact of such frameworks on alleviating inefficiency, unreliability, and non-scalability. The paper combines leading edge technologies with strong data driven decision making to present actionable feedback on exploiting test beds to catalyse IoT innovation against pivotal challenges including interoperability, security, and scalability.

articleTitle: Modeling Recalls for Automobiles
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Managing the product recalls in automotive industry is a crucial and relevant problem which impacts human lives and ensures secure operation of automobiles. Recalls of products deals with withdrawing vulnerable products from the marketplace, thus optimizing the corporate's liability for their negligence. The existing techniques and technologies available for product recall management has a deficit of transparency showing recall data patterns depicting the recall urgency derived from its potential risks. This study provides a structured approach which reveals patterns inherent in recall data and classifies the recalls based on its potential risks. The outcome offers relevant insights for manufacturers and regulatory bodies, facilitating in improving the recall management processes and strengthen public safety by treating critical vehicle defects within proper timeline.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Approaches for Brain Stroke Detection: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Stroke is one of the leading causes of death in adults around the world and demands prompt and accurate diagnosis to start treatment in time. In these directions, there are recent progress in deep learning such as CNNs, transfer learning methods, and a variety of hybrid models, which are quite promising to be highly relevant for the detection and, even, prediction of brain stroke. Two broad areas form this framework: analysis of medical images (CT, MRI) and real-time bio-signal processing (EEG). Despite all this, there is still room for improvement-for example, requiring large diverse datasets, providing an outcome to address class imbalances, and ensuring models generalize well. Deep learning in conjunction with clinical expertise can greatly help improve the detection and prediction of stroke, thus shortening treatment times and allowing more favorable patient outcomes. Further research is necessary to bypass these limitations and eventually realize its full potentials.

articleTitle: Analyzing Financial Metrics: A Comparative Study of Salesforce and Microsoft Dynamics 365
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The purpose of the study is, therefore, in the integration of six variables consisting of closing prices, daily returns, volatility, stock prices together with moving averages, trading volumes, and their moving averages: how these measure interrelates and what impacts they have toward market sentiment. Correlation and regression tests were carried out to ascertain whether the obtained findings were reliable enough to present robust relationships among the metrics of concern. Therefore, the obtained findings have wider implications for investors, as well as their investing decisions. In the first place, these findings permit one to detail and analyze in an in-depth manner the stock shares' behavior overtime and variations of the market so that trends within trading activity could be unearthed and understood long-term effects.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Early Identification of Diseases in Tomato Leaf Crops
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Early disease identification is essential for prevention in tomato leaf crops and to reduce crop loss. Unfortunately, traditional manual methods are very timeconsuming and error-prone making automated solutions necessary. This study aims to use deep learning, leading the way using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for disease detection in tomato leaves. Experiments on image classification were conducted for three different models (such as ResNet50, VGG16 and an upgraded version of VGG19) Proposed VGG19 model is giving superior performance, with an accuracy of 99.5%, precision: 99.23 % and recall :99.47% F1-Score: 99.28%. At the other end of the scale, ResNet101 and ResNet50 also performed quite well but with a little less accuracy percentage while VGG16 came at last. The results reveals that the Proposed VGG19 model is highly efficient for early disease detection in tomato crops and can be a powerful tool over precision agriculture.

articleTitle: Real-Time Sign Language Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Sign language is the primary mode of communication for deaf and hard of hearing community. This paper discusses the development of a real time sign language recognition system by deploying deep learning techniques. For instance, the aim is to establish a good model which could be used to identify different hand gestures as used in sign languages. Once trained on a data set of 10 different hand gestures, the system is able to recognize and predict gestures in other images. The use of TensorFlow and Keras in the implementation ensures scalability of the system for real-time application. This method aims at assisting the deaf and mute people by developing an application that will improve their social life. Furthermore, TensorFlow and Python facilitate the porting of the system to mobile and embedded systems, which enhance its reach among different gadgets. This system is intended to help avoid one of the main concerns of sign language users in which they have limited ability to interact with others and thus limited engagement with basic services. The objective of the researcher is to make the quality of life of sign language users better by translating their gestures into a format that is easier to understand.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Survey of Post-Quantum Secure Lattice-Based Authentication Schemes for VANETs
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) rely heavily on Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) to enable secure and reliable communication between vehicles and roadside infrastructure. However, Shor's algorithm poses a significant threat to conventional cryptographic systems. To counteract this threat, post-quantum cryptography offers quantum-resistant solutions capable of providing secure authentication in the face of quantum adversaries. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of recently proposed six post-quantum state-of-the-art authentication protocols designed to meet the security and performance demands of VANETs. The survey identifies key strengths and limitations in existing approaches, providing valuable insights to guide future research in designing robust, efficient, and quantum-resistant authentication mechanisms for next-generation vehicular networks.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Skin Cancer Detection Merging CNNs with Vision Transformers
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Skin cancer is one of the top health concerns globally, and early detection is essential to ensure good patient outcomes. Earlier research studies have applied CNNs or Vision Transformers separately, and CNNs outperform on local feature extraction, whereas ViTs are more successful in capturing global dependencies. However, such isolated techniques suffer from limitations such as lower accuracy on heterogeneous datasets and poor generalization. This work bridges this gap by introducing a hybrid model that synergizes the strengths of both architectures. The CNN extracts low-level details like textures and edges, while the ViT captures spatial relationships across the image. Evaluated on open-source skin cancer datasets, the proposed model outperforms individual approaches in accuracy, reliability, and generalization, making it a robust tool to assist dermatologists in early stage diagnosis.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Satellite Images for Anomaly Identification in Patterns
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Anomaly detection in remotely sensed imagery constitutes a pivotal endeavor with a multitude of applications, encompassing areas such as environmental surveillance and precision agriculture. A variety of methodologies have been formulated to augment the identification of anomalies, defined as deviations from anticipated patterns within image datasets. These approaches capitalize on sophisticated computational strategies and advanced machine learning algorithms to enhance both accuracy and operational efficiency. Anomaly detection in remotely sensed imagery can be implemented through an array of techniques, including heterogeneous and Edge Computing (EC), CNN, feature spaces with multi-dimensionality, unified anomaly detection frameworks, and unsupervised learning for the identification of burnt areas, among others. This manuscript elucidates various methodologies and state-of-the-art technologies pertinent to anomaly detection. Although each of these methodologies exhibits significant advancements, obstacles and constraints continue to exist pertaining to the requirements for digital assets and the imperative for real-time processing functionalities. Subsequent study endeavors may prioritize the refinement of these models to enable more extensive applications and to improve their flexibility in accommodating emerging data sources.

articleTitle: Smart Garden Watering and Lighting System Integrated with Machine Learning Model to Maintain Urban Gardens
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Garden maintenance may be a difficult task, particularly in urban settings. Many people are not skilled enough to determine their plants’ precise requirements for lighting and watering. Conventional gardening techniques frequently result in underwatering or overwatering, wasting resources, and producing unhealthy plants. Our completely automated smart garden watering and lighting system offers a fully automated solution to these problems. With its sophisticated sensors, this system keeps an eye on the quantity of moisture in the soil and the amount of sunshine it receives, making sure plants get the correct amount of both for healthy growth. Traditional gardening involves guesswork and physical effort, which our solution avoids by automating the irrigation and lighting operations. You may have the advantages of a flourishing garden without the trouble of ongoing upkeep with our intelligent gardening system. Our method offers a dependable and effective solution to care for your plants and improve your urban green space, regardless of experience level.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Techniques for Object Detection in Underwater Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The degradation of image quality caused by things like light absorption, scattering, and distortion makes object detection in underwater environments a unique challenge. Applications like marine research, environmental monitoring, and autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) are restricted in their effectiveness by traditional image processing techniques, which often struggle with these complexities. Recent years have seen the rise of deep learning techniques as a potent weapon in the fight against these obstacles. In order to accurately detect objects underwater, this paper investigates the use of deep learning models, specifically convolutional neural networks (CNNs). We explore cutting-edge models and methods like attention mechanisms, transfer learning, and hybrid deep learning architectures to improve detection performance in challenging underwater environments. Furthermore, we utilize data augmentation techniques and synthetic dataset generation to tackle the critical issue of limited labeled underwater datasets. From a detection accuracy and robustness perspective, the experimental results show that our suggested deep learning method is light years ahead of the competition. Marine exploration, autonomous underwater vehicle navigation, and underwater surveillance systems can all benefit from this study's new insights into how to better detect objects in real time while submerged.

articleTitle: Bi-GRU and Glove Based Aspect-Level Movie Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of deep learning architectures for sentiment analysis in text-based data. The methodology begins with data collection, where movie reviews sourced from IMDb are utilized, reflecting a variety of emotional expressions. The dataset undergoes preprocessing, which includes tokenization, embedding using GloVe, and splitting into training and testing sets, with 80 allocated for training and 20 for testing to ensure reliable model evaluation. The models implemented in this study include GRU with GloVe embeddings, BiGRU with GloVe embeddings, and LSTM with GloVe embeddings. Each model is constructed to capture sequential dependencies in the text, allowing for a nuanced understanding of sentiment. The models are compiled with appropriate optimizers and loss functions, and their performance is evaluated using accuracy, precision, and recall metrics. During the testing phase, the trained models are assessed based on their ability to classify sentiments effectively, generating insights into their performance. The results are visualized to highlight misclassification and areas for improvement. This methodology streamlines the sentiment classification process, reducing reliance on manual analysis and enhancing overall efficiency. The findings demonstrate that deep learning models can significantly improve sentiment analysis accuracy, providing valuable insights for future research in emotion detection within Natural Language Processing (NLP) applications.

articleTitle: A Transparent Diagnosis Model for Diabetic Retinopathy Using Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy is the leading cause of vision problems and partial blindness, and its signs are complicated and variable, making detection difficult. Standard diagnosis is mainly reliant on expert interpretation of retinal images, which can lead to bias and mistake, highlighting the need for improved diagnostic approaches. Despite the fact that conventional AI technologies considerably improve diagnostic skills, their black box aspect limits healthcare practitioners' confidence and optimizes their usage in practice. Grad-CAM++ is a new technique that addresses the black box problem by improving model knowledge, allowing users to grasp the reasoning behind specific decisions. Using XAI approaches, this work creates a diagnostic model for diagnosing diabetic retinopathy, hence improving transparency. The proposed model's convergent plots validate the learning process, which results in 94.4% better diagnostic precision than previous approaches.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Object Detection for Autonomous Vehicles: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Object detection is an integral piece of autonomous cars learning their surroundings and making safe judgements about where and how to drive in real time. This research compares and contrasts multiple machine learning models for object identification in autonomous cars in order to assess accuracy, computational economy, and real time performance. Then, we present how various well known proposed models (CNN, YOLO, SSD, R-CNN) perform in changing driving conditions. It researches the models capabilities to run real time applications within autonomous cars, as well as the trade off of speed and accuracy between different models. We also study how hyperparameter adjustment, data augmentation and transfer learning impact these models’ performance. Through thorough research on benchmark datasets, this work shows the benefits of the adoption of hybrid models, which mix speed and accuracy, to increase item recognition in real world contexts. This study contributes to the expanding corpus of knowledge on AI driven solutions for autonomous systems by having useful insights regarding the improvement of autonomous vehicle object identification algorithms.

articleTitle: Advances in Big Data and Data Mining: Techniques and Applications in Data Fusion for Enhanced Insights and Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The advancement of big data has accelerated over the years to change how companies utilize data to drive decisions. And so, this paper aims to look at big data and data mining in different perspectives while highlighting the importance of data fusion in decision making in the current society. Many times, data fusion combines different data sources to provide better and broader results. Clustering of raw data, anomaly detection and machine learning are discussed as well as their use in healthcare, financial management and smart cities. This paper also presents such issues as data heterogeneity, data quality assurance, as well as scalability issues. Lastly, tomorrow's possibilities, such as artificial intelligence and quantum computing, are presented as possible enhancements of the data fusion effectiveness are mentioned due to the expected marked advancement in real-time and adaptive decisionmaking systems.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Clinical Decision Support Systems: Revolutionizing Healthcare With Predictive Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSS) is changing the face of healthcare by allowing AI powered predictive, data driven insights, enabling medical practitioners to prolong their diagnosis and treatment planning. To make better and faster clinical judgements, CDSS based on AI using machine learning techniques such as ensemble methods and deep learning is discussed in this paper. He said most of the focus is on models that can predict future events, diagnose plagues and deliver tailored treatment programs sifting through mountains of health care data, such as genetics, medical imaging and EHRs. Some of the main problems we work with as we implement AI driven CDSS is its data privacy, model interpretability and integration to current healthcare processes. In addition this study summarizes recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), enabling real time analysis and making real time decisions to improve patient outcomes and reduce workloads of healthcare personnel. Case examples that employ AI-CDSS to identify diseases, optimize treatments and predict risk are provided to show how they can change the face of clinical practice. Finally, we explore where AI healthcare may be going from here with a focus on the importance of deploying these systems with patient well being in mind and with full compliance to the relevant regulations.

articleTitle: Natural Disaster Prediction Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Accurate prediction techniques are essential in an era when natural disasters pose severe dangers to human lives and infrastructure. This article presents a deep learning approach that uses convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to anticipate natural disasters such as floods, earthquakes, wildfires, and storms. The work preprocesses a dataset of 4,429 pictures using scaling, normalization, and augmentation techniques (such as flipping and rotation) to ensure model resilience and diversity in the data. The image sets were separated into training, validation, and test sets to optimize model performance. Several CNN architectures were used to train the model, including Xception, VGG16, and MobileNet. The testing results showed that MobileNet outperformed the other models with a test accuracy of 92.25%. VGG16 finished second with 91.50%, while Xception achieved 91.00%. A thorough performance assessment was produced by examining these models according to precision, recall, and F1 score. The impressive outcomes, especially for MobileNet, are ascribed to its capacity to effectively extract salient characteristics from the pictures, like distinct patterns and textures connected to different kinds of calamities. The study's overall findings demonstrate that CNN-based models can make precise predictions about natural disasters in real-time situations. To improve early warning systems, the models in this work indicate a high degree of accuracy by merging image data from satellite sources and using advanced data augmentation techniques. The results show how deep learning can practically enhance emergency preparedness and response procedures.

articleTitle: IoT Based Smart and Precise Autonomous Irrigation Management System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: Traditional irrigation methods are highly inefficient, labor intensive, and results in water wastage. Additionally unpredicted weather, unanticipated rainfalls could compromise the crop health. Addressing all the challenges the proposed IoT system automates the irrigation by using real-time data such as rainfall, soil-moisture, humidity, temperature and crop area and sends to a python-based engine, which calculates water requirement, controls the water pumps in the fields through microcontroller NodeMCU, provides the required water to the crop. By doing so, the system not only conserves the water but also reduces the labor costs, prevents under- or over-irrigation, increases the crop productivity, promotes the sustainable farming practices. The updates regarding the irrigation can be viewed by the web application controlled by the python-engine. The system is versatile, suitable for open fields, aeroponic towers, gardens, small farms and research purposes. The desired objective is to reduce the water consumption by 40% and labor cost by 90%, make the irrigation efficient and reduce cost.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis on Severity Estimation of Plant Diseases by Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The rapid spread of diseases and pest infestations has a detrimental effect on plant health. Methods for disease classification and detection have gained new insights from the developments in computer vision and deep learning approaches. However, there has been relatively limited work in the area of severity estimation and disease progression rate since it requires more detailed information such as the percentage of affected leaf area, symptoms intensity, and environmental factors that lead to the disease progression over time. Thus the modern agricultural sector faces a significant difficulty in the assessment of plant disease severity and tracking of disease development. The purpose of this study is to perform a thorough review of various deep learning methods for plant disease severity assessment, taking into account factors like accuracy, severity level measurement, and dataset employed. The article also suggests ways to address the shortcomings of the current approach.

articleTitle: H-Shaped Multi-Analyte PCF-Integrated SPR Sensor For Multi-Industry Fluid Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: This research conducts a numerical investigation of a multi-analyte H-patterned photonic crystal fiber (PCF) sensor utilizing surface plasmon resonance (SPR) technology developed to recognize industrial fluids in various medical and chemical applications efficiently. The sensor incorporates two fluid channels, simultaneously detecting multiple analytes. It uses a gold-titanium dioxidecoated plasmonic layer, providing high sensitivity, improved electric field confinement, and chemical stability. The sensor is optimized for refractive index ranges of 1.34-1.38 in channel-I and 1.39-1.43 in channel-II, both with high accuracy. This study aims to develop a platform for real-time analyte monitoring. The Finite Element Method is applied for arithmetical assessment after refining the sensor's architectural parameters. The sensor demonstrates a peak wavelength sensitivityof 4,000 nm/RIU in channel-I and 28,000 nm/RIU in channel-II. Additionally, it achieves maximum amplitude sensitivitiesof <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{410.64 }\text{RIU}^{-1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1561.55 \text{RIU}^{-1}$</tex> in the respective channels. This corresponds to a resolution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.5 \times 10^{-{6}}$</tex> RIU for channel-I and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.57\times 10^{-7}$</tex> RIU for channel-II. This sensor is designed to detect unknown substances with RIs between 1.34 and 1.43, making it valuable for biological fluid diagnosis, food quality control, environmental monitoring, and chemical analysis.

articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning for Early Detection of Cardiovascular Diseases
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: In order to enhance patient outcomes, rapid and precise detection approaches are needed for cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), which are among the top causes of death globally. By examining a wide range of demographic and clinical data, this study investigates how machine learning approaches could improve the early diagnosis of CVDs. We explore how many different machine learning methods could identify different heart diseases. Decision trees, support vector machines and more, are included in these algorithms. By using feature selection and optimization methods we want to strengthen these models' prediction abilities and make them more resilient. The dataset used by this research includes all of the medical information of patients as they include all the pertinent biomarkers such as age, blood pressure, cholesterol levels and etc. The results suggest that machine learning models, especially ensemble methods like Random Forest and gradient boosting, are indeed able to predict the risk of CVD better than conventional diagnostic strategies. Results suggest that early risk assessment using machine learning embedded within healthcare processes is a reliable and non-invasive approach. This study has found machine learning to have promise for change and further research into the practical use of these models to revolutionize treatment of cardiovascular diseases.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Identification and Diagnosis Using YOLOv10
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: The field of medical imaging has been greatly impacted in recent years by developments in deep learning and artificial intelligence, especially in the detection and diagnosis of brain tumours. In order to improve the accuracy and efficiency of brain tumour diagnosis on MRI scans, this research explores the possibilities of YOLOv10 (You Only Look Once), an inventive object detection algorithm. YOLOv10 differs from conventional segmentation techniques in that it incorporates state-of-the-art neural network architectures to offer real-time cancer region detection and classification. We investigate how well the model performs in relation to the most advanced methods currently in use across a range of parameters, including false positive/negative rates, processing speed, and detection accuracy. Our results show that YOLOv10 performs better in localising tumour boundaries while undergoing rigorous testing on a sizable dataset of annotated MRI images. Brain tumors present a major challenge to patients and the medical community, requiring novel strategies for accurate diagnosis and early identification. This journal article examines the state-of-the-art discoveries at the nexus of neuroscience and medicine that have transformed the area of diagnosing and detecting brain tumors.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Real Time Semantic Segmentation of Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computational, Communication and Information Technology (ICCCIT)
abstract: This research presents an innovative navigation framework designed for autonomous vehicles. It integrates advanced deep learning models ResNet50, U-Net, and Efficient- NetBO to address real-time semantic segmentation challenges in dynamic driving environments. The framework is tailored to enhance the vehicle's capacity to interpret complex surroundings with minimal human guidance. The ResNet50 model serves as the primary feature extractor, capturing intricate spatial information from high-resolution camera feeds, which aids in accurately detecting critical elements like lane boundaries, pedestrians, and road signs. U-Net then performs pixel-level segmentation, enabling a detailed understanding of the scene by categorizing each image segment. EfficientN etBO is integrated to optimize the balance between model precision and computational speed, ensuring real-time performance essential for autonomous driving. This architecture supports robust decision-making capabilities, allowing for precise tasks such as obstacle detection, lane maintenance, and dynamic path planning, even in complex, shifting scenarios. By combining the unique strengths of these models, the framework surpasses the limitations of traditional navigation methods, improving the safety, dependability, and overall efficacy of autonomous systems. The use of advanced semantic segmentation within this approach has the potential to propel autonomous technology forward, enabling more intelligent and adaptive vehicles.

articleTitle: Impact of Cryptocurrency on Global Financial Stability: Analyze Regulatory Responses and Their Effectiveness in Managing Risks Associated with Cryptocurrencies
